`POST /v1/hooks/{hookId}/test` sends a realistic (or your own pasted) alert through the real pipeline as a **paper** order
and answers with the outcome. Alerts refused at the door (unreadable, stale, queue full) and rejected orders are announced on the event bus as
`hook.rejected` for notifiers, and refusals are audited as `hook.refused` (without the body, at most once a minute per hook and kind).

---

<!-- docs/guides/webhooks.md -->

# Alerts: TradingView, signed generic hooks, ChartInk and GoCharting

An alert from your own code or a charting site becomes an order through a **hook**: a URL with a secret token, tied
to one account and a set of limits. Every signal goes through the same safety checks, rate limits, idempotency and
audit log as an order sent from a script. Hooks are **paper** by default.

Four sources are supported:

| Source | Sender | Credential |
|---|---|---|
| `tradingview` | TradingView alerts | URL token **plus** a passphrase inside the alert message (TradingView cannot sign) |
| `generic` | Your own scripts, bots and services | URL token **plus** an HMAC signature on every request |
| `chartink` | ChartInk scan alerts | URL token only (ChartInk cannot sign) |
| `gocharting` | GoCharting alerts | URL token only (GoCharting cannot sign) |

The dashboard does the same as the API below: **Integrations → Webhooks → Create webhook** (choose the source there;
it defaults to TradingView). For TradingView alerts go to [TradingView](#tradingview); the rest of this page covers
every source.

## TradingView

A TradingView alert can place a **paper** order through a `tradingview` hook. TradingView cannot sign a request, so the
hook is protected by three things together: the secret address, a **passphrase** written inside the alert message, and
(optionally) TradingView's published sender addresses. Alerts older than a limit you set are refused, a repeat of an
alert is never placed twice, and nothing the alert says can make the Bridge do more than the hook allows.

### What TradingView does (checked against TradingView's own pages)

Checked on **2026-11-09**. TradingView can change any of this; the Bridge does not depend on the items marked "not
documented".

| Fact | What TradingView says | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Two-step sign-in | Webhook alerts are only allowed when 2-factor authentication is enabled on your TradingView account | [About webhooks](https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000529348-about-webhooks/) |
| Plan | The help page does not name a plan. TradingView's pricing page lists webhook notifications as a feature of its paid plans (not verified here which plan from which tier: check the pricing page for your account) | [Pricing](https://www.tradingview.com/pricing/) |
| Ports | Only ports 80 and 443 are accepted; other ports are rejected | About webhooks |
| Time allowed | If the server takes longer than **three seconds**, the request is cancelled | About webhooks |
| Retries | **Not documented.** The page says a webhook may occasionally fail to arrive and points to the alert log's "Webhook status" column. Assume TradingView does not resend: the Bridge answers at once and never relies on a resend | About webhooks |
| Message and content type | The alert message is the request body. If it is valid JSON, TradingView sends `Content-Type: application/json`; otherwise `text/plain` | About webhooks |
| Headers and signing | The help page describes no way to add a header or sign the request. The Bridge therefore uses a passphrase inside the message | About webhooks |
| Sender addresses | 52.89.214.238, 34.212.75.30, 54.218.53.128, 52.32.178.7 | About webhooks |
| IPv6 | Not supported for webhooks | About webhooks |
| Time placeholders | `{{timenow}}` is the moment the alert fires, `{{time}}` the start of the bar; both are UTC, written like `2019-08-27T09:56:00Z`, to the nearest second | [Variables in alerts](https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000531021-how-to-use-a-variable-value-in-alert/) |
| Other placeholders | `{{ticker}}`, `{{exchange}}`, `{{close}}`, `{{interval}}`; for strategies `{{strategy.order.action}}` (buy or sell), `{{strategy.order.contracts}}`, `{{strategy.order.price}}`, `{{strategy.order.id}}`, `{{strategy.market_position}}` (long, flat or short), `{{strategy.market_position_size}}` (never negative) | Variables in alerts |
| Placeholders in Pine | In Pine's `alert()` the message is plain text you build yourself with `str.tostring()`; placeholders work in the alert dialog's Message box, not inside `alert()` or a strategy's `alert_message` | [Pine alerts](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/alerts/) |
| Not documented | Message size limit, whether redirects are followed, the User-Agent, how the reply body is used | |

What the Bridge does about the gaps: it accepts a body of up to 16 KB, answers `202` within milliseconds (well inside
three seconds), and treats an identical alert it has already seen as a duplicate, so a resend, if TradingView ever
sends one, cannot place a second order.

### Set it up

1. **Make the hook.** Dashboard: API, Integrations, Webhooks, choose **TradingView**, then **Create webhook**. Copy the
   **webhook address** and the **passphrase** now; the Bridge keeps only a fingerprint of each and cannot show them
   again. (The same from the API: `POST /v1/hooks` with `"source": "tradingview"`.)
2. **Give TradingView an address on the internet.** `http://127.0.0.1:4300/...` only works on this computer. Follow
   [Exposing alerts safely](expose-alerts.md); you end with an address like `https://alerts.example.com`. Type it into
   the dashboard form (or the box under the new hook) and it shows the final address to paste. The final address is
   that address followed by the hook's path: `https://alerts.example.com/hooks/tradingview/<token>`. It must use port
   80 or 443.
3. **Create the alert in TradingView.** Open a chart, then the alarm-clock icon (or Alt+A).
   - Choose the condition (an indicator, a strategy, or a price level).
   - Notifications tab: tick **Webhook URL** and paste the address.
   - Settings tab: replace the whole **Message** box with one of the messages below, with your passphrase in it.
   - Create the alert.
4. **Check it.** In the dashboard, open **Alerts** on the hook and choose **Send a test alert**: the Bridge runs a
   realistic alert through the same checks and places a paper order. A test proves the hook works; it does not prove that
   TradingView can reach it. When a real alert fires, it appears in the same list within seconds. Hooks that have never
   heard anything, or have been quiet for days, say so there.

### The alert message

JSON is easiest. Numbers such as `{{close}}` stay **without quotes**; text placeholders have quotes. TradingView fills
the placeholders in, then sends the result as JSON.

**Indicator or price alert:**

```
{
  "symbol": "{{exchange}}:{{ticker}}",
  "side": "buy",
  "lots": 1,
  "orderType": "limit",
  "price": {{close}},
  "product": "MIS",
  "mode": "paper",
  "id": "my-alert",
  "time": "{{timenow}}",
  "passphrase": "YOUR_PASSPHRASE"
}
```

**Strategy alert** (every order fill; TradingView fills in the action, size, price and position):

```
{
  "symbol": "{{exchange}}:{{ticker}}",
  "side": "{{strategy.order.action}}",
  "lots": {{strategy.order.contracts}},
  "orderType": "limit",
  "price": {{strategy.order.price}},
  "product": "MIS",
  "mode": "paper",
  "marketPosition": "{{strategy.market_position}}",
  "positionSize": {{strategy.market_position_size}},
  "id": "{{strategy.order.id}}",
  "time": "{{timenow}}",
  "passphrase": "YOUR_PASSPHRASE"
}
```

**Plain text** also works (TradingView then sends `text/plain`): one order, side first, then the symbol and size, then
the rest in any order:

```
BUY {{exchange}}:{{ticker}} 1 @ {{close}} MIS mode=paper id=my-alert time={{timenow}} passphrase=YOUR_PASSPHRASE
```

The dashboard prints these with your real passphrase and your hook's order type and product already filled in
(`MARKET` hooks leave out `price`; a hook that fixes the product leaves out `product`).

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `symbol` | The chart ticker with its exchange, `{{exchange}}:{{ticker}}`. A name with no exchange is refused: the same name can exist on two exchanges, and the Bridge never guesses |
| `side` | `buy` or `sell` (not `long`, `short` or `exit`). Left out only when the hook fixes the side |
| `lots` or `quantity` | Not both. For futures and options `{{strategy.order.contracts}}` counts lots, so send it as `lots`. For shares, 1 lot is 1 share. If both are left out the order is one lot |
| `orderType` | `limit` or `market`; must match the hook. A LIMIT hook needs `price` |
| `product` | `CNC`, `INTRADAY`, `MARGIN`, or the broker words `MIS` (INTRADAY), `NRML` (MARGIN), `DELIVERY`, `CARRYFORWARD`. If the hook fixes a product, a different one is refused |
| `account` | Optional. Must be the hook's own account |
| `mode` | `paper` (the default when left out) or `live`. Must equal the hook's mode |
| `marketPosition`, `positionSize` | Strategy alerts. Recorded with the alert and shown in the list; the order is the buy or sell TradingView sent. The Bridge does not net positions in this version |
| `time` | `{{timenow}}`. Used for the age limit and as part of the alert's identity. Required on a live hook |
| `id` | Your alert's name or `{{strategy.order.id}}`. With `time`, `symbol` and `side` it is the alert's identity |
| `passphrase` | The hook's passphrase, in the message. Never shown again, never logged |

Any other field refuses the alert (`quantiy` is refused, not read as a one-lot order). So does an unfilled
`{{placeholder}}`, a bad number, or JSON that is not valid JSON (the reply names what is wrong).

**Pine `alert()` (indicator).** Placeholders do not work inside `alert()`: build the text yourself with
`str.tostring()`, as below. Test the time format in the Pine Editor before relying on it.

```pine
//@version=6
indicator("Breakout alert", overlay = true)
breakout = ta.crossover(close, ta.sma(close, 20))
nowUtc = str.format_time(timenow, "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss", "UTC") + "Z"
if breakout
    alert('{"symbol": "' + syminfo.prefix + ':' + syminfo.ticker + '", "side": "buy", "lots": 1, "orderType": "limit", "price": ' + str.tostring(close) + ', "product": "MIS", "mode": "paper", "id": "breakout", "time": "' + nowUtc + '", "passphrase": "YOUR_PASSPHRASE"}', alert.freq_once_per_bar_close)
```

**Pine strategy.** The simplest way is the strategy template above in the alert's Message box (placeholders work there).
To send different text per order, give the order an `alert_message` and put `{{strategy.order.alert_message}}` in the
Message box; the text in `alert_message` is built in Pine like the indicator example, and an order without one sends an
empty message (which the Bridge refuses with a clear reason).

### Names: chart tickers, products

The Bridge reads the alert's symbol the way a chart writes it (the `from=chart` mapping) and refuses anything it cannot
map to exactly one instrument.

| In TradingView | Bridge symbol | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NSE:RELIANCE` | `NSE:RELIANCE` | cash |
| `NSE:M_M`, `NSE:BAJAJ_AUTO` | `NSE:M&M`, `NSE:BAJAJ-AUTO` | charts write `_` where the exchange writes `&` or `-` |
| `NSE:NIFTY1!`, `NSE:NIFTY2!` | the nearest and the next NIFTY future (`NFO:NIFTY-...-FUT`) | resolved from the instrument master when the alert arrives; quantity must be a multiple of the lot size, so send `lots` |
| `NSE:NIFTY261027C25000` | `NFO:NIFTY-2026-10-27-25000-CE` | option written as YYMMDD, C or P, strike (the Bridge's reading of the chart form; check it with a test alert on your symbol) |
| `NFO:NIFTY-2026-10-27-FUT` | unchanged | a full Bridge symbol is accepted as is |
| `RELIANCE` (no exchange) | refused | send `{{exchange}}:{{ticker}}` |
| `NSE:NIFTY` | refused when the order is placed | an index cannot be traded |

Products: `MIS` = `INTRADAY`, `NRML` = `MARGIN`, `CNC` = delivery. An unknown ticker is accepted by the receiver and then
**rejected after the 202** (`SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND`); it shows in the hook's Alerts list with the reason.

A continuous future (`NIFTY1!`) rolls to a new contract at expiry; a hook with `allowedSymbols` lists exact contracts and
must be updated at each roll (the create response warns 7 days ahead).

### What protects a TradingView hook

| Protection | What it does |
|---|---|
| Secret address | A 256-bit token in the URL; only its hash is stored |
| Passphrase | In the message; 128 random bits, shown once, stored hashed, compared in constant time. A wrong one is `401`; 30 wrong ones a minute from one address answer `429` |
| Sender addresses | `"sourceIpPreset": "tradingview"` accepts only the four TradingView addresses above, plus any in `allowSourceIps` and the global `hooks.allowSourceIps`. Behind a tunnel the Bridge sees the tunnel, not TradingView: set `hooks.clientIpHeader` (`cf-connecting-ip` for Cloudflare Tunnel; trusted only when the connection comes from this computer) or every alert is refused |
| Age limit | `maxAgeSec` (default 120): an alert whose `time` is older is refused as stale, one more than a minute in the future too. If fresh alerts are refused, check this computer's clock |
| No double orders | An alert is identified by `id` + `time` + `symbol` + `side`: a resend is acknowledged as a duplicate and places nothing. The memory is a small file in your data folder (`hooks-seen.json`, bounded, hashes only), so a restart does not forget. The order itself carries a derived `clientOrderId` (`mcb-<hook>-<hash>`) and a stable Idempotency-Key, so even a lost memory cannot place the same alert twice that day |
| Burst of alerts | Orders are paced by the account's order-rate cap. An alert that meets it waits (queued, up to `hooks.burstWaitSec`, 30 by default) and is placed when a slot frees up, instead of being refused; past that wait, or when the queue (`hooks.queueSize`) is full, it is refused with a clear reason and nothing is placed |
| The hook's own limits | Account, allowed symbols, lots cap, product, order type and side are fixed on the hook; everything else is refused, never trimmed |
| Paper first | Alerts are paper unless the hook is live. A paper hook refuses an alert that says `"mode": "live"` |

**Live TradingView hooks.** Everything above, plus: creating one needs the `live` scope, live enabled for the account in
the config, and one of `sourceIpPreset`/`allowSourceIps`, `requireConfirmation` or `acknowledgeUnsignedLive`; it must
have `maxAgeSec`; every alert must say `"mode": "live"` and carry its `time`; and the key that created it must still
exist. An alert without `"mode": "live"` means paper, so a live hook refuses it. With `requireConfirmation` the alert
only opens a ticket that you confirm on this computer. A test alert is always a paper order.

### Where to look when it does not work

Dashboard: **API, Integrations, Webhooks, Alerts** on the hook. Every alert that reached the hook is there with what
happened to it; wrong passphrases and refused addresses are counted at the top. The same from the API:
`GET /v1/hooks/{hookId}/signals`. The audit log (`hook.signal`, `hook.refused`) keeps the permanent record.

| What you see | Likely cause and what to do |
|---|---|
| Nothing in Alerts, and TradingView's alert log says it fired | The alert never reached the Bridge. Check the address in the alert's Webhook URL box (the path must include `/hooks/tradingview/`), that the tunnel is running and `server.publicIngress.allowedHosts` has its host, that the port is 80 or 443, and TradingView's own "Webhook status" in its alert log. Try the test alert, then `curl` the address from another network |
| "1 wrong passphrase" counted | The message has no passphrase or the wrong one. Copy the message again from the dashboard |
| "from an address that is not allowed" counted | You turned on the TradingView address list and the Bridge sees another address. Behind a tunnel set `hooks.clientIpHeader`; if TradingView changed its addresses, edit `hooks.presets.tradingview` |
| Unreadable | The reason says what: an unfilled `{{placeholder}}` (the placeholder is in a place TradingView does not fill, for example a strategy placeholder in a plain alert), invalid JSON (quote text placeholders, leave numbers bare), an unknown field, a missing exchange |
| Too old | The alert's `time` is older than `maxAgeSec`. Use `{{timenow}}`, not `{{time}}` (the bar's start). If every alert is too old, check this computer's clock |
| Not placed, reason shown | The alert arrived and the order was refused: an unknown symbol, over the lots cap, the product or order type differs from the hook, a limit price too far from the market, the kill switch, a closed market, the account cannot trade. Nothing was placed |
| Placed but you expected a live order | The hook is paper. Alerts on a paper hook never place live orders |
| Needs you | The hook requires confirmation: confirm the ticket in the dashboard (Orders, Pending confirmations) within a minute |
| TradingView says the alert timed out | The Bridge answers in milliseconds, so the delay is the tunnel or the network. Do not resend by hand: check the Alerts list first; if it arrived, it is there |

A rejected order after the `202` is announced on the Bridge's event bus as `hook.rejected` (a notifier such as Telegram
can deliver it), and is in the audit log. Wrong passphrases and refused addresses are counted and audited (at most
once a minute per hook), never announced.

### Settings for TradingView hooks

Per hook (`POST /v1/hooks`): `source: "tradingview"`, `maxAgeSec` (5 to 3600, default 120), `sourceIpPreset`
(`"tradingview"`). In the config file, section `hooks`:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `clientIpHeader` | `null` | Header that carries the real sender address behind a local tunnel |
| `presets.tradingview` | built in | `{ "ips": [...], "verifiedAt": "2026-11-09", "source": "https://..." }`: the address list, shown in the dashboard and by `GET /v1/hooks/presets`; edit it when TradingView's page changes |
| `burstWaitSec` | `30` | How long an alert may wait for an order-rate slot; `0` turns waiting off |
| `signalsKept` | `100` | Alerts remembered per hook for the Alerts list (memory only) |
| `dedupeWindowMs`, `queueSize`, `maxSignalsPerMinute` | as in the config reference | |


## 1. Create a hook

Admin key, from this computer:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/hooks -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCB_ADMIN_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "source": "generic",
  "label": "NIFTY breakout",
  "account": "paper",
  "mode": "paper",
  "product": "MARGIN",
  "orderType": "LIMIT",
  "maxLotsPerSignal": 2,
  "allowedSymbols": ["NFO:NIFTY-2026-10-27-FUT"],
  "requireConfirmation": false
}'
```

The reply holds `url` and `path` (with the token; **shown once**, only a hash is kept), for `generic` hooks a
`signingSecret` and for `tradingview` hooks a `passphrase` (also shown once), ready-to-paste `templates` for the alert message, and any `warnings`. `GET /v1/hooks` lists hooks without tokens; `DELETE /v1/hooks/{hookId}`
stops a URL at once.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `source` | `tradingview`, `generic`, `chartink` or `gocharting` |
| `account` | The account orders go to |
| `mode` | `paper` (default) or `live`. Creating a live hook is refused unless the creating key has the `live` scope as well as `admin`, the account has `live.enabled` and `"webhook"` in its `live.allowedSources`, `safety.liveTrading` is on, and (for unsigned sources, see below) one of `allowSourceIps`, `requireConfirmation` or `acknowledgeUnsignedLive` is set |
| `side` | Fix the side (`BUY`/`SELL`). Required for ChartInk, whose alerts carry none; otherwise an alert asking for the other side is refused |
| `product`, `orderType` | Fixed per hook (`LIMIT` alerts must carry a price) |
| `maxLotsPerSignal` | Larger signals are refused, never trimmed |
| `allowedSymbols` | Only these canonical symbols (recommended for derivatives). Exact contracts: a dated future stops matching on expiry, so the create response warns 7 days ahead; update the hook at each roll-over |
| `requireConfirmation` | Every signal waits on the dashboard (Pending confirmations); confirming places exactly that order, once; declining ends the signal as `rejected` (`TICKET_REJECTED`) and nothing is sent |
| `allowSourceIps` | Optional allowlist of sender IP addresses or IPv4 CIDR blocks (for example the addresses your alert service publishes) |
| `sourceIpPreset` | `"tradingview"`: also accept alerts only from TradingView's published addresses (the editable list in the config, see [TradingView](#tradingview)) |
| `maxAgeSec` | Refuse an alert whose own `time` is older than this many seconds (5 to 3600). TradingView hooks default to 120 and a live one must have it; for other sources it applies when the alert carries a `time` written like `2026-11-09T09:56:00Z` |
| `acknowledgeUnsignedLive` | `true` to accept that a live ChartInk, GoCharting or TradingView hook is protected by its URL (and passphrase) alone (audited and shown on the hook) |

**Unsigned live hooks: the trade-off.** ChartInk, GoCharting and TradingView cannot sign their alerts, so the URL
token is the only credential, and that URL lives in your charting account, browser history and tunnel logs. Replay
protection is only the dedupe window. For `"mode": "live"` the Bridge therefore insists on at least one extra guard:
`allowSourceIps` or `sourceIpPreset` (best, when the service publishes its sending addresses), `requireConfirmation: true` (you approve each
order), or an explicit `acknowledgeUnsignedLive: true`. Signed `generic` hooks (HMAC with a timestamp) need none of
these. The key that created a live hook is recorded on it; revoke that key and the hook stops accepting alerts.

## 2. Make the URL reachable

TradingView, ChartInk and GoCharting post from the internet (TradingView only to port 80 or 443), and so does any script running
elsewhere. The full walk-through, with a safe tunnel, is [Exposing alerts safely](expose-alerts.md); in short: Turn on the **public ingress** listener, which serves `/hooks/*` and nothing else, and run your own tunnel
to it:

```json
"server": { "publicIngress": { "enabled": true, "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 4301, "allowedHosts": ["hooks.example.com"] } }
```

```bash
cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:4301     # or a named tunnel with your own host name
```

`mc-bridge expose alerts` does this (and the host list, the client-address header and a TradingView sender allowlist) in one
step and checks the result: see [expose-alerts.md](expose-alerts.md).

Give the sender `https://<tunnel host>/hooks/<source>/<token>` (the `path` from step 1). If the tunnel runs on this
computer and adds a client-IP header, set `hooks.clientIpHeader` so IP allowlists see the real sender (trusted only from loopback).

## 3. Alert messages

### Signed generic hook (your own code)

The recommended source for anything you control.

`"source": "generic"` returns a `signingSecret` (shown once). Sign each request:

```python
import hmac, hashlib, json, time, urllib.request

body = json.dumps({"symbol": "NSE:RELIANCE", "side": "BUY", "quantity": 1, "orderType": "MARKET", "id": "sig-42"}).encode()
t = str(int(time.time()))
sig = hmac.new(SECRET.encode(), t.encode() + b"." + body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
req = urllib.request.Request(HOOK_URL, data=body, method="POST",
                             headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "X-MCB-Signature": f"t={t},v1={sig}"})
print(urllib.request.urlopen(req).read())
```

Requests older or newer than 5 minutes, or replayed inside that window, are refused with `401` before the body is
read. `{ "signals": [...], "id": "batch-7" }` sends several at once.

The body accepts `symbol` (any symbol the Bridge understands, canonical preferred), `side`, `quantity` or `lots`,
`price` (required for `LIMIT` hooks), `orderType`, `product`, and `id` (+ optional `time`). Reusing an `id` the same
day never creates a second order. When the body also carries `time`, the identity is `id` **and** `time`: a sender that
reuses one id every day (a strategy order id such as `Long`) still gets a new order for each new time.

### ChartInk

Create the hook with `"source": "chartink"` and a fixed `"side"`. Paste the URL into the scan's webhook box. ChartInk
sends its standard JSON (`stocks`, `trigger_prices`, `triggered_at`, `scan_name`); each stock becomes one signal of one
lot (one share for cash) at most, up to the per-alert cap.

### GoCharting

`"source": "gocharting"`; the alert text uses the plain-text grammar, for example `SELL NSE:SBIN 5 MKT INTRADAY` or
`BUY NSE:RELIANCE 10 @ 1402.5 id=L1 time=2026-10-19T04:00:00Z`. A JSON message works too. When the message carries
both `id` and `time`, a double delivery (or a re-delivery the same day) places **one** order; otherwise identical
messages inside `hooks.dedupeWindowMs` count as one. Words the Bridge does not understand, or an unfilled
`{{placeholder}}`, refuse the alert instead of guessing. Use `allowedSymbols` on derivative hooks.

## 4. What happens to a signal

`queued` → `processing` → `placed` | `duplicate` | `awaiting_confirmation` | `rejected` | `failed` |
`outcome_unknown`. Each step is in the audit log as `hook.signal` with the hook id, symbol, order id and reason. A
full queue answers `429` with a message that says so (never unbounded); each hook is limited to
`hooks.maxSignalsPerMinute`. The kill switch refuses every signal. An order that meets the account's order-rate cap
waits for a free slot (`hooks.burstWaitSec`) instead of being refused.

`GET /v1/hooks/{hookId}/signals` lists the recent alerts of a hook (newest first, at most `hooks.signalsKept`, memory
only) with an `outcome` (`placed`, `queued`, `awaiting_confirmation`, `duplicate`, `stale`, `rejected`, `refused`,
`failed`, `outcome_unknown`, `dropped`), a plain-words `summary`, the reason and the order id, plus counts that also
include wrong passphrases and refused addresses (counted, never listed, never with a body).
`POST /v1/hooks/{hookId}/test` sends a realistic (or your own pasted) alert through the real pipeline as a **paper** order
and answers with the outcome. Alerts refused at the door (unreadable, stale, queue full) and rejected orders are announced on the event bus as
`hook.rejected` for notifiers, and refusals are audited as `hook.refused` (without the body, at most once a minute per hook and kind).

---

<!-- docs/guides/alert-orders.md -->

# Orders for alerts, sheets and scripts

Strategy alerts, spreadsheets and Telegram bots do not say "buy 1 share". They say "be long 3 lots", "send these two
orders together", "is the market open?" and "can I afford this?". This guide covers the routes that answer those, and
the small conveniences that let people type what they are used to. Every route here is in
[openapi.yaml](../openapi.yaml). Examples use the demo Bridge on port 4300 and a key in `$KEY`.

Everything below keeps the rules of [safety.md](safety.md): paper unless you ask for live, every order passes the same
checks as `POST /v1/orders`, and an AI assistant's order still needs a person to confirm it on this computer.

## Words the order routes understand

On `POST /v1/orders`, `/v1/orders/preview`, `/v1/orders/to-target`, `/v1/orders/batch` and `/v1/margin/basket` you can write
the words people already use. The Bridge reads them, uses the canonical word and tells you in `meta.normalised`.

| You write | The Bridge uses | Field |
|---|---|---|
| `MIS` | `INTRADAY` | `product` |
| `NRML`, `CARRYFORWARD` | `MARGIN` | `product` |
| `DELIVERY` | `CNC` | `product` |
| `CNC`, `MTF` | unchanged | `product` |
| `MKT` | `MARKET` | `orderType` |
| `SLM`, `SL_M`, `STOP_LOSS_MARKET` | `SL-M` | `orderType` |
| `STOPLOSS`, `STOP_LOSS` | `SL` | `orderType` |
| `buy`, `sell`, `limit`, `day`, `ioc` | upper case | `side`, `orderType`, `validity` |

Case does not matter. A word that is not on this list is refused as before. `mode` is never rewritten: `"live"` must be
written exactly like that.

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/orders -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"account":"demo-paper","symbol":"NSE:M_M","side":"BUY","quantity":1,"product":"MIS","orderType":"MARKET"}'
# 201  "symbol":"NSE:M&M"  "product":"INTRADAY"  meta: "normalised":[{"field":"product","from":"MIS","to":"INTRADAY"}]
```

Symbols are read more loosely too. These all resolve in every route that takes a symbol:

| You write | The Bridge uses |
|---|---|
| `NSE:M_M`, `NSE:BAJAJ_AUTO` (chart tools spell `M&M` and `BAJAJ-AUTO` this way) | `NSE:M&M`, `NSE:BAJAJ-AUTO` |
| `NSE_INDEX:NIFTY 50`, `NSE:NIFTY BANK` | `NSE:NIFTY`, `NSE:BANKNIFTY` |
| `NSE_EQ:RELIANCE`, `NSE:RELIANCE-EQ` | `NSE:RELIANCE` |
| `NSE_FO:NIFTY-2026-11-24-FUT` | `NFO:NIFTY-2026-11-24-FUT` |
| `NSE:NIFTY1!` (chart continuous future) | the nearest `NFO:NIFTY-<expiry>-FUT` |

A `_` is turned into `&` or `-` only when the result is a real instrument in your broker's list. If two different
instruments could be meant, the answer is `AMBIGUOUS_SYMBOL`, not a guess.

## Check a symbol: `/v1/symbols/validate` and `/v1/symbols/resolve`

For a sheet or an alert author who wants to see what the Bridge will do with what they typed.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/symbols/validate?symbol=NSE:BAJAJ_AUTO"
```
```json
{"data":{"input":"NSE:BAJAJ_AUTO","valid":true,"symbol":"NSE:BAJAJ-AUTO","exchange":"NSE","kind":"EQ","lotSize":1,"tickSize":0.1,
 "tradable":true,"normalised":true,"rules":["chart name NSE:BAJAJ_AUTO read as NSE:BAJAJ-AUTO"],"confidence":"exact"}}
```

`validate` never fails for a bad symbol. It answers `"valid": false` with `code` (`SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND`,
`AMBIGUOUS_SYMBOL`) and the closest `candidates`. `POST /v1/symbols/validate` with `{"items":[{"symbol":"..."}, ...]}`
checks up to 200 in one call. An index shows `"tradable": false`.

`GET /v1/symbols/resolve?q=...&exchange=...&explain=1` answers one instrument for free text such as `Reliance`,
`NSE:M_M` or `NIFTY BANK`, with the rule it used and ranked `candidates`, each with the reason it matched. It never guesses:

- a bare name resolves to the cash or index instrument when exactly one has that name;
- two with the same name (the same share on NSE and BSE) is **409 `AMBIGUOUS_SYMBOL`** with the candidates in the
  problem body. Send `exchange=NSE` or the full symbol;
- a name that is only a prefix is **404 `SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND`** with the closest names;
- a future or option is never picked from a bare name; send its full symbol.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/symbols/resolve?q=RELIANCE&kind=FUT&limit=3"
# 409  {"code":"AMBIGUOUS_SYMBOL","candidates":[{"symbol":"NFO:RELIANCE-2026-11-23-FUT","lotSize":525,"reason":"exact name match, future on NFO"}, ...],
#       "rule":"3 contracts carry this name; send the full contract symbol"}
```

## Be at a target size: `POST /v1/orders/to-target`

A strategy alert says "be long 3 lots", not "buy 1". This route reads the position, works out the difference and
places only that.

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/orders/to-target -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: alert-0001" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"account":"demo-paper","symbol":"NSE:INFY","targetQuantity":7,"product":"MIS","orderType":"MARKET"}'
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `targetQuantity` or `targetLots` | The size to end at, signed: `7` long, `0` flat, `-50` short. Send one of them. |
| `account`, `symbol`, `product`, `orderType`, `price`, `triggerPrice`, `validity`, `tag`, `clientOrderId`, `mode` | As on `POST /v1/orders`. Paper unless `"mode": "live"`. |
| `dryRun` | `true`: work it out and run every check, place nothing. The reply has the `preview`. |
| `openOrders` | `"refuse"` (default) or `"ignore"`, see below. |

The reply: `currentQuantity`, `targetQuantity`, `delta`, `action` (`BUY`, `SELL` or `NONE`), `placed`, the `order` (or
`null`) and, for a dry run, the `preview`. `201` when an order was placed, `200` when nothing was needed.

```json
{"data":{"account":"demo-paper","symbol":"NSE:INFY","product":"INTRADAY","mode":"paper","currentQuantity":0,"targetQuantity":7,
 "delta":7,"action":"BUY","dryRun":false,"placed":true,"order":{"orderId":"PAPER-20261109-000002","side":"BUY","quantity":7,"status":"filled"}}}
```

Rules that keep it safe:

- **An unknown position places nothing.** If the positions cannot be read, or a row cannot be matched with certainty,
  the answer is `503 POSITION_UNKNOWN` ("retryable": no order was sent, so it is safe to send again). Unknown is never
  treated as flat. A live position row the Bridge cannot name but whose text contains your symbol also counts as unknown.
- **The position is for this symbol and this product.** An `INTRADAY` target is measured against the `INTRADAY` position.
  Positions in other products are listed in `otherProducts`, never added.
- **Live delivery** (`CNC`, `MTF`): shares can appear in both today's positions and the holdings. If both show the
  symbol, the answer is `POSITION_UNKNOWN`, because the Bridge cannot tell whether they are the same shares. If only one
  shows it, that one is used.
- **Open orders.** An order of the Bridge in the same symbol and product that is still open (a MARKET or LIMIT order, or
  a partly filled one) could change the position when it fills, so the request is refused with `409 STATE_CONFLICT`
  unless you send `"openOrders": "ignore"`. A resting stop (`SL`, `SL-M`) does not block. Only the Bridge's own orders
  are known; an order you placed in the broker's app is not.
- **Same gates as `POST /v1/orders`.** The delta order goes through the same order service: kill switch, safety limits,
  price and tick checks, live opt-ins, order-rate caps, market orders policy, and the human confirmation for AI assistants
  (use `dryRun` to open the ticket, then send again with the `confirmToken`). There is no other way in.
- **Idempotency.** The `Idempotency-Key` (or `clientOrderId`) covers the whole request. Sending it again with the same
  body returns the first answer (with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`), even if the position has changed since, including
  "nothing to do". The same key with another body is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Two requests for the same account,
  symbol and product are handled one after the other. The record is kept in memory for 24 hours; after a restart the
  order inside is still protected by its own saved key. A live request needs the key or a `clientOrderId`.
- A move through zero (long 3 to short 2) is one order of 5.

## Several orders at once: `POST /v1/orders/batch`

A convenience for an alert that needs two legs (a hedge and a main order). It is not a strategy engine: the legs do not
know about each other, nothing is rolled back, and a leg that is refused does not undo the others.

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/orders/batch -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: batch-0001" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"account":"demo-paper","orders":[
        {"symbol":"NSE:INFY","side":"BUY","quantity":1,"product":"MIS","orderType":"MARKET"},
        {"symbol":"NSE:NOPE","side":"BUY","quantity":1,"product":"MIS","orderType":"MARKET"}]}'
```
```json
{"data":{"ok":false,"summary":{"total":2,"placed":1,"rejected":1,"outcomeUnknown":0,"skipped":0},"results":[
  {"index":0,"ok":true,"status":"placed","orderId":"PAPER-20261109-000003","idempotencyKey":"batch-0001:0","order":{"...":"..."}},
  {"index":1,"ok":false,"status":"rejected","error":{"code":"SYMBOL_NOT_FOUND","status":404,"retryable":false,"message":"..."}}]}}
```

- Up to **20** orders. Each is an ordinary order body without `account` (the account is at the top; a leg may repeat it).
  A batch-level `mode` applies to legs that do not set their own.
- Legs run one after another in the order sent (`"legOrder": "buys-first"` sends the buys first). **`results` is always in
  the order sent**, one entry per leg, each with its own `status`: `placed`, `rejected`, `outcome_unknown` (check the order
  book before sending it again) or `skipped`.
- **Nothing is hidden in the status code.** `201` only when every leg was placed. `207` when at least one leg went out (or
  may have) and at least one did not. `422` when no leg went out. `data.ok` and `data.summary` say the same. A client that
  accepts any 2xx must read `data.ok`.
- `"stopOnError": true` stops after the first leg that did not go out; the rest show `skipped`.
- **Idempotency per leg:** leg `i` uses your `Idempotency-Key` plus `:i` (`batch-0001:1`), so a leg cannot be placed twice even
  if the whole request is retried. The same key and body returns the first answer. A batch where nothing went out can be
  retried with the same key; one where something went out is answered from the record, so to retry only the failed legs use a
  new key. A live leg needs the key (or its own `clientOrderId`).
- Every leg passes the same checks as a single order, including the kill switch and the live opt-ins, one leg at a time.
  More than 20 legs, no legs or a body that is not a list are refused before anything is sent.

## What will it cost: `POST /v1/margin/basket`

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/margin/basket -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"positions":[{"symbol":"NFO:NIFTY-2026-11-23-FUT","side":"BUY","lots":1,"product":"NRML"}]}'
```
```json
{"data":{"total":177192.01,"span":144975.28,"exposure":32216.73,"hedgeBenefit":0,"source":"paper-model","account":"demo-paper","legs":1,
 "note":"Paper model: approximate, not the exchange's SPAN."}}
```

Up to 50 positions; all figures are JSON numbers in rupees; a read-only key may call it; nothing is placed.
`source` says where the figure came from:

- `broker`: the broker's own calculator, used when the account's adapter has the optional `fetchBasketMargin(creds, legs)`.
  No shipped adapter has it yet, so this is for adapters to add (needs a check against each broker's own documentation).
- `paper-model`: the paper engine's approximate portfolio model ([paper-margin.md](paper-margin.md)), for the basket on its own with
  hedges between its legs counted. It is **not** the exchange's SPAN, and `note` says so. When the broker call failed, the
  note says that too.

`account` is optional: without it a paper account your key may use is taken. `hedgeBenefit` is what the legs would need
alone minus `total`. The compat `margin` call (`/api/v1/margin`) answers from the same calculation.

## Is the market open: `/v1/calendar/*`

Read-only answers from the holiday list shipped with the Bridge (NSE and BSE circulars). NFO follows NSE, BFO follows BSE.
MCX and CDS have their own hours that the list does not hold (`422`).

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/calendar/status?exchange=NSE"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/calendar/sessions?exchange=NSE&date=2026-11-10"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/calendar/holidays?exchange=NSE&year=2026"
```

- `status`: `open`, `pre-open` or `closed`, the reason (a holiday is named), when it closes or opens, and the next open
  (a special session such as Muhurat trading counts). `closedBecause` is `weekend`, `holiday`, `before-open` or `after-close`.
- `sessions`: whether a date is a trading day, why not, pre-open, open and close in IST, a special session if any, and the
  neighbouring trading days.
- `holidays`: every row with its own `verified` flag, and the special sessions of the year.

**Verified or not is said in every answer** (`calendar.verified`, `calendar.note`). The list is dated (`calendar.asOf`) and
covers the years in `calendar.coveredYears`. A date outside them is treated as an ordinary weekday and marked
`covered: false`, `verified: false` with a plain note: it is "no data", not "no holiday". The pre-open, open and close times
are the standard hours and are marked `sessionTimes.verified: false`. This is the calendar's answer, not the exchange's live
state: a halt or an unlisted closure is not in it. Check the exchange's circular before relying on a date.

### For spreadsheet authors

`server/bridge/market/calendarView.mjs` exports `createCalendarView({ now })`. Its `cell(exchange, field)` returns one plain
value for a cell: `status`, `reason`, `opensAt`, `closesAt`, `nextOpen`, `isTradingDay`, `holiday` or `verified`. Times are IST
text, and a value that does not exist is an empty string, never a guess. A spreadsheet route can call it and answer with
the value as `text/plain`, like the other `/xl` routes.

---

<!-- docs/guides/telegram.md -->

# Telegram: alerts on your phone, and prices when you ask

The Bridge can send you a short Telegram message when something needs you (an order was rejected, a broker is logged
out, the kill switch went on) and can answer a few **read-only** questions: prices, positions, orders, funds, status.

It needs a Telegram account and a bot you make yourself (two minutes, free). The Bridge talks to Telegram only from this
computer, outward: no port is opened, no tunnel, no webhook.

Set it up in the dashboard: **API, Integrations, Telegram**. Or in a terminal: `mc-bridge notify telegram setup`.

## What it does, and what it never does

| It does | It never does |
|---|---|
| Sends alerts for the events you switch on (table below) | Place, change or cancel an order |
| Answers `/price`, `/positions`, `/orders`, `/funds`, `/status`, `/help` to chats you allowed | Approve an order that is waiting for you |
| Sends a morning reminder when a broker account is not logged in | Create or revoke an API key |
| Lets you turn the **kill switch on** with `/kill` and a one-time code | Release the kill switch (that is only possible on this computer) |

**Why there are no approve buttons.** An order that needs a person is approved with a single-use token, by an admin key,
from this computer. That is on purpose. A Telegram account can be taken over (a SIM swap, a stolen unlocked phone, a
hijacked session), Telegram chats are not end-to-end encrypted by default, and a forwarded message or a stale button
would be enough to confirm real money. So the Bridge tells you in Telegram that an order is waiting, and you approve it
on the computer. Orders from Telegram, from TradingView and from spreadsheets never approve themselves.

## Set it up

### 1. Make a bot with BotFather

1. In Telegram, search for **@BotFather** (the official bot with a blue tick) and press Start.
2. Send `/newbot`.
3. Choose a name (anything, for example "My Bridge") and a username that ends in `bot` (for example `my_bridge_123_bot`).
4. BotFather replies with a **token**: a long text like `123456789:ABC...`. Anyone who has it can control the bot, so
   treat it like a password. If it leaks, send `/token` to BotFather to get a new one.

### 2. Give the token to the Bridge, on this computer

Dashboard: **API, Integrations, Telegram**, paste the token, press **Check and save**. The Bridge asks Telegram whether the
token is real, then keeps it **encrypted on this computer** (the same store as your broker login values). It is never
shown again, never written to a log, and never sent anywhere except to Telegram.

Terminal: `mc-bridge notify telegram setup`. The token is asked for with hidden input; it is never an argument (a
command line stays in your shell history and in the process list). It needs an admin key: `MCB_ADMIN_KEY` in the
environment, or `--key`.

The token can only be entered on this computer. The routes that take it refuse requests from anywhere else.

### 3. Find your chat

A bot cannot write to you until you write to it first.

1. In Telegram, open your new bot and press **Start** (or send any message).
2. In the dashboard press **Find my chat**. The Bridge reads your message and shows the chat's name, its type and the last
   four digits of its id. Press **Use this chat** to confirm.

Only chats you confirm here ever get alerts. A message from any other chat is **ignored without a reply** and only
counted (the status line shows "N messages from other chats ignored"), so a stranger who finds your bot learns nothing.

A **private chat** may also ask for prices and status. A **group** receives alerts but may not ask for anything until you
switch that on (everyone in the group could type commands). In a group the bot only sees commands that name it
(`/price@my_bridge_123_bot NIFTY`) while Telegram's privacy mode is on, which is the default.

### 4. Choose what you get, and send a test

Tick the events you want (the defaults are sensible), then press **Send a test message**. The result says delivered, or what
is wrong, in plain words.

## Which events

All are on or off in the dashboard (or `PUT /v1/notify/events`). Messages are plain text, short, with rupees written the Indian way.

| Event | Default | Example message |
|---|---|---|
| An order is rejected | on | `Order rejected: SELL 5 INFY (live, Dhan Main). Reason: Insufficient margin.` |
| An order's result is not known | on, always sent | `Order result unknown: BUY 1 RELIANCE on Dhan Main. The broker did not confirm it: check your broker. Do not send it again; the Bridge is checking the order book.` |
| An order is filled | on | `Filled: BUY 10 RELIANCE at ₹2,431.50 (paper, Paper).` |
| An order is placed | off | `Order placed: BUY 10 RELIANCE (paper, Paper).` |
| An order needs your approval | on | `An order is waiting for your approval: BUY 10 RELIANCE (about ₹24,315) on Dhan Main. Approve it ON THIS COMPUTER, in the Bridge dashboard, within about a minute. It cannot be approved from Telegram.` |
| The kill switch is turned on | on, always sent | `Kill switch ON (by Telegram): manual. New orders are blocked until you release it on this computer.` |
| The kill switch is turned off | on | `Kill switch OFF. Orders can be sent again.` |
| A broker account is logged out | on | `Dhan Main is logged out. Log in again on this computer, or prices and orders from it stop.` |
| An account cannot trade (or can again) | on | the readiness check's own sentence |
| A webhook alert is rejected | on | `A webhook alert was rejected on "NIFTY scalp" (BUY INFY). Reason: Symbol is not on the hook's allowed list.` |
| A webhook alert arrived too late | on | `A webhook alert arrived too late and was dropped on "NIFTY scalp".` |
| A webhook alert failed after it was accepted | on | `A webhook alert was accepted but its order failed on "NIFTY scalp". Reason: ...` |
| A daily safety limit is reached | on | `Daily loss limit reached on Dhan Main: ₹5,200 against a limit of ₹5,000. New orders on it are blocked for today.` |
| A data source is switched off after failures | on | `Data source NSE end of day is paused after repeated failures. The Bridge tries it again by itself.` |
| Many requests are slowed by rate limits | on | `Rate limits slowed 23 requests in the last 10 minutes. Most of it on Dhan Main (quote). Prices may lag a little; nothing is lost.` |
| Morning reminder to log in | on | `2 accounts are not logged in: Zerodha Main, Dhan Main. Log in on this computer before the market opens at 09:15.` |
| End-of-day summary | off | one line per account: orders, fills, rejections, P&L |

An order whose result is unknown is never called "failed": it may well have reached the exchange. The message says
"unknown, check your broker".

There is no event for backup results: the Bridge has no backup job today.

**What is never in a message:** a bot token, an API key, an order confirmation token, a webhook address, a broker password
or a session value. Every message is scrubbed for anything shaped like those before it is queued, and a test checks it.

### Reminders and quiet hours

- **Morning reminder:** at 08:45 IST on trading days, "N accounts are not logged in" with their names; a second nudge at
  09:10 if they still are. Nothing is sent when everything is logged in, on weekends, or on an exchange holiday (the
  holiday list shipped with the Bridge, `server/bridge/reference/data/holidays.json`; a day it does not know is judged by
  weekday). A special session (Muhurat trading) has its own hours, so no reminder is sent that day. A Bridge started at
  14:00 does not send the 08:45 reminder late. The times can be changed.
- **End-of-day summary:** optional, 15:45 IST: orders, fills, rejections and profit or loss per account, paper and live
  kept apart.
- **Quiet hours:** off by default. When on (for example 22:00 to 07:00 IST), everyday alerts are held and arrive as one
  message when quiet hours end. The kill switch and unknown order results are never held.
- **Bursts:** if ten orders are rejected in a few seconds you get the first one at once, then one line, "9 more (an order is
  rejected) in the last 20 seconds. Latest: ...". The same text again within a minute is counted, not sent.

## Commands

Send these from a chat you switched commands on for. They only read.

| Command | What you get |
|---|---|
| `/price NIFTY RELIANCE` | A price for each symbol, with its **data class and delay**: `NIFTY 24,880.50 (+0.42%) - real-time, 2 s ago`, or `RELIANCE 2,431.50 - delayed 15 min, unofficial`. A bare symbol means NSE; write `BSE:SENSEX` for another exchange. Up to 10 symbols. |
| `/positions` | Open positions per account (paper and live), with profit or loss |
| `/orders` | The latest orders, with plain status words |
| `/funds` | Cash and margin per account |
| `/status` | Which accounts are logged in, whether the kill switch is on, and how the data sources are doing |
| `/help` | The list |
| `/kill` | Turn the kill switch on. The bot replies with a short code; send `/kill 4821` (your code) within 60 seconds. The code works once, three wrong tries cancel it, and it only turns the switch **on**. Open orders are not cancelled. |

A price is never shown without how fresh it is. A delayed, end-of-day or unofficial number carries that word. Those numbers
never feed orders, risk checks, paper fills or alerts: they are for you to read.

Commands are limited to 10 per minute per chat (a setting). A command that waited more than two minutes (the Bridge was
off) is ignored, so an old message never runs later. Every command is written to the audit log with the chat's short key,
never its id.

## The safety stance, in one place

- The bot token and your chat ids are typed on this computer only, stored encrypted, masked everywhere (screens show four
  characters of the token and the last four digits of a chat id), and never logged.
- Alerts go only to chats you confirmed. Commands are answered only to chats you allowed for commands. Everyone else is
  ignored silently and counted.
- Commands read through a read-only key made for this: it can see prices, positions, orders and funds, nothing else.
- The only action from Telegram is **kill switch on**, after a one-time code. Releasing it is not possible from Telegram.
- Telegram sees the text of the messages you ask for (prices, positions, orders). Do not add the bot to a chat with people
  you would not show your positions to. Telegram chats are not end-to-end encrypted.
- The Bridge connects only to `api.telegram.org`, over HTTPS, with certificate checks. There is no setting to point it elsewhere.

## When Telegram is slow or down

Messages wait in a small file on this computer (`notify/outbox.json` in the data folder) and survive a restart. The Bridge
retries with growing pauses (2 s, 4 s, 8 s ... up to 5 minutes, six tries), waits exactly as long as Telegram says when it
asks the Bridge to slow down, never sends to one chat faster than about once a second, keeps a group under 18 messages a
minute and the whole bot under 20 a second, and drops a message that is more than an hour old rather than delivering stale
news. The queue holds at most 200 messages; when full the oldest ordinary one goes first. All of these are settings
(`notify` in `bridge.config.json`, see [notifications.md](notifications.md)).

## Telegram's limits (from Telegram's own documentation)

Checked on 2026-11-09 against Telegram's official pages. Numbers Telegram does not publish are marked.

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| One chat: avoid more than **one message per second**; short bursts may pass, but going on eventually gives `429` errors | [Bots FAQ](https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq) |
| A group: no more than **20 messages per minute** | Bots FAQ |
| Broadcasting: about **30 messages per second** across users, unless paid broadcasts are enabled (up to 1000 per second, 0.1 Star per message over the free 30, needs a large balance and audience) | Bots FAQ |
| A flood-control error carries `parameters.retry_after`: the seconds to wait before trying again | [Bot API, ResponseParameters](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api) |
| A group that became a supergroup answers with `parameters.migrate_to_chat_id` | Bot API |
| `sendMessage` text: **1 to 4096 characters** after entity parsing (the Bridge cuts at 4000 and sends plain text, so nothing needs escaping) | Bot API, `sendMessage` |
| `getUpdates` is long polling: `timeout` is the seconds to hold the request, `limit` 1 to 100, `offset` confirms what was read; unread updates are kept at most **24 hours**; it does not work while a webhook is set | Bot API, `getUpdates` |
| A failed request has `ok: false`, a `description` and an integer `error_code`, whose "contents are subject to change in the future" | Bot API |
| Privacy mode is on by default: in groups the bot sees only commands that name it, replies to it and a few more; it sees all messages in private chats | [Bots FAQ](https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq), [Bot features](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features) |
| `/newbot` makes a bot; the token "can be used by anyone to control your bot"; `/token` makes a new one | [Bot features](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features) |
| Chat ids fit in 52 bits; the Bridge keeps them as text | Bot API |

**Not promised by Telegram's documentation** (seen in practice, so the Bridge treats these only as hints and maps them to
plain words): the exact `error_code` and `description` for a rejected token (usually 401), a chat that blocked the bot
(usually 403 "bot was blocked by the user"), another program reading the same bot (409 "Conflict") and an unknown chat
(400 "chat not found"); and that a person must press Start before a bot can write to them. If Telegram changes a wording, the
worst case is the generic message "Telegram refused the request" instead of a specific one; nothing is sent twice because of it.

## Troubleshooting

**It went quiet.** Open the Telegram card or run `mc-bridge notify status`. The health line says why, in plain words:
- *Telegram does not accept this bot token*: BotFather's `/token` gave a new one, or the bot was deleted. Paste the new token (Change token).
- *This chat has blocked the bot*: open the chat and press Start again, or add the bot back to the group. Then send a test.
- *Telegram asked the Bridge to slow down*: it waits by itself; the status shows how long.
- *Could not reach Telegram*: check this computer's internet or VPN. Messages wait and are sent when it is back (up to an hour).
- Nothing is wrong but nothing arrives: check the event is switched on, that quiet hours are not holding it, and that a chat is on the list.

**I am being flooded.** Switch off the chatty events (An order is placed, An order is filled), turn quiet hours on, or raise
the rate-limit alert threshold. A burst already arrives as one digest line. If a webhook sends hundreds of bad alerts, fix the
alert or delete the hook; "A webhook alert is rejected" is merged into digests too.

**The bot does not answer my commands.** Is the chat on the list with commands switched on (private chats are on by
default, groups off)? In a group, address the bot (`/price@my_bridge_123_bot NIFTY`) or make it an admin. Is the command
older than two minutes? Did you send more than 10 in a minute? A chat that is not on the list is never answered, by design.

**"Another program is already reading this bot's messages."** Telegram allows one reader per bot. Another copy of the Bridge,
a script or a webhook is using the same token. Stop it, or make a second bot for the Bridge.

**The token ended up somewhere it should not be** (a screenshot, a chat, a shell history). Send `/token` to BotFather for a
new one, then change it in the Bridge. The old one stops working at once.

**The time is wrong.** Times in the card and the messages are IST. The morning reminder uses the shipped holiday list; if an
exchange holiday is missing, update the Bridge: the list is refreshed with each release.

## Settings

See [notifications.md](notifications.md) for the `notify` section of `bridge.config.json` and the routes.

---

<!-- docs/guides/notifications.md -->

# Notifications: how the Bridge tells you things

The Bridge listens to its own events (orders, tickets, the kill switch, broker sessions, webhook alerts, safety limits,
data sources) and turns the ones you chose into short plain messages. Today the way to receive them is
**Telegram**: see the step-by-step [Telegram guide](telegram.md). This page is the reference: how a message travels, the
settings, and the routes.

## How a message travels

```
event on the Bridge's bus
  -> is this event switched on?                         (PUT /v1/notify/events, defaults in the table of telegram.md)
  -> same text a moment ago? count it, do not send       (dedupe, 60 s)
  -> a burst of the same kind? first at once, rest merged (one digest line, 20 s)
  -> quiet hours? hold it, send with the others later    (critical events skip this)
  -> outbox: a file on disk, bounded, survives restart
  -> pacing: one chat about once a second, a group under 18 a minute, the bot under 20 a second
  -> Telegram sendMessage, plain text
       failure: retry with growing pauses; "slow down" from Telegram: wait exactly that long;
       a bad token or a blocked chat: stop, say so in plain words
```

Nothing here can change what the Bridge does: notifications only observe. If Telegram is down, orders, prices and safety
checks are unaffected.

Delayed, end-of-day and unofficial data never feed alerts or orders. A `/price` answer shows such data only with its
label (see [sources.md](sources.md)).

## Settings

Everything has a default. `bridge.config.json`, section `notify` (all optional):

```json
"notify": {
  "enabled": true,
  "events": { "order.placed": true, "hook.stale": false },
  "quietHours": { "enabled": false, "start": "22:00", "end": "07:00" },
  "morning": { "enabled": true, "at": "08:45", "secondAt": "09:10", "endOfDay": { "enabled": false, "at": "15:45" } },
  "coalesceSeconds": 20,
  "dedupeSeconds": 60,
  "rateLimitAlert": { "threshold": 20, "windowMinutes": 10 },
  "pacing": { "perChatMs": 1100, "perSecond": 20, "groupPerMinute": 18 },
  "retry": { "maxAttempts": 6, "baseMs": 2000, "maxMs": 300000, "maxAgeMinutes": 60 },
  "queue": { "max": 200 },
  "inbound": { "enabled": true, "commandsPerMinute": 10, "pollSeconds": 25, "allowKill": true, "maxCommandAgeSeconds": 120 }
}
```

| Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `events` | Event key to on or off. Keys are in the table of [telegram.md](telegram.md). What you save in the dashboard wins over the file. |
| `quietHours`, `morning` | Times are IST, 24-hour `"HH:MM"`. `morning.enabled` and `morning.endOfDay.enabled` only choose where the two reminder switches start. |
| `coalesceSeconds`, `dedupeSeconds` | Burst window and duplicate window. `0` switches that off. |
| `rateLimitAlert` | The "many requests are slowed by rate limits" message is sent once when `threshold` slowed requests happen within `windowMinutes`. |
| `pacing` | Telegram's documented limits are one message per second per chat, 20 a minute to a group, about 30 a second for a bot. These defaults stay under them. They are settings because Telegram may change them. |
| `retry` | Tries, first pause, longest pause, and how old a message may get before it is dropped instead of sent late. |
| `queue.max` | The outbox holds at most this many messages. |
| `inbound.enabled` | Switch off to stop listening for commands (alerts still go out). |
| `inbound.allowKill` | Whether `/kill` can turn the kill switch on. Releasing from Telegram is never possible. |

The bot token and the chat ids are **not** settings: they are entered on this computer (dashboard, or `mc-bridge notify
telegram setup`) and kept encrypted.

## Files

All under the data folder, `notify/` (mode 0600, written atomically): `outbox.json` (messages waiting), `state.json` (what
Telegram last said, poll position, reminders already sent, today's counters), `settings.json` (the events you chose).
The token and chat ids are in the encrypted secret store (`secrets.enc`), names `notify:telegram:<id>`. If `outbox.json`
cannot be read it is moved aside as `outbox.json.corrupt-<time>` and the Bridge starts with an empty outbox.

## Routes

All need an admin key. Everything that changes something or sends a message is **this computer only**; the three reads
(`status`, `targets`, `events`) are admin only. No response contains a token or a chat id: only a token hint (four
characters), the bot name, a chat name, the last four digits of a chat id and a short chat key. Full shapes are in
[openapi.yaml](../openapi.yaml) (tag Notifications).

| Route | Does |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/notify/status` | Queue depth, last delivery, last error per target (plain words), counters, quiet hours, next reminder |
| `GET /v1/notify/targets` | Bots and their chats, masked |
| `POST /v1/notify/targets` | `{ "token": "..." }`: checks it with Telegram, stores it encrypted. The same bot with a new token replaces the token |
| `DELETE /v1/notify/targets/{id}` | Forget the bot, its token, its chats and its queued messages |
| `POST /v1/notify/targets/{id}/test` | Send a test message; reports delivery per chat |
| `POST /v1/notify/targets/{id}/find-chat` | Chats that wrote to the bot recently, to confirm |
| `POST /v1/notify/targets/{id}/chats` | `{ "ref" }` (from find-chat) or `{ "chatId", "name" }`, optional `commands` |
| `PATCH` / `DELETE /v1/notify/targets/{id}/chats/{key}` | Allow or stop commands from a chat / remove it |
| `GET` / `PUT /v1/notify/events` | The events with labels and whether each is on / change them, quiet hours and reminder times |

Terminal: `mc-bridge notify telegram setup | remove <id>`, `mc-bridge notify status`, `mc-bridge notify test`. `mc-bridge
doctor` reports Telegram truthfully: not set up, set up but never delivered (unverified), delivering (with the time), or
cannot send (with the reason). It makes no network call; it reports what the running Bridge last saw.

## For module authors: events the notify module listens to

Bus topics (`server/bridge/core/eventBus.mjs`): `order.updated`, `order.outcome_unknown`, `ticket.prepared`,
`safety.kill_switch`, `safety.limit`, `account.status`, `trading.readiness` (when `notify: true`), `limits.throttled`,
and `hook.rejected`, `hook.stale`, `hook.failed` for a webhook alert that was accepted with 202 and then did not become an
order (payload: `label`, `hookId`, `source`, `reason`, optional `symbol` and `side`). A module can also queue its own
message with `deps.notify.publish({ key, text, group })`; it goes through the same switches, dedupe and quiet hours. A
payload must never carry a secret; messages are scrubbed anyway.

---

<!-- docs/guides/recording.md -->

# Recording: save prices and option chains as they happen

Brokers give you old candles, but they do not give you old option chains, old open-interest snapshots or old tick-by-tick prices. If you want those later, someone has to write them down while the market is open. The recorder does that for you, from the Bridge's own live data, into plain files on this computer.

- It saves **real-time data only**. If the only answer available is delayed or end-of-day, the recorder does not write it. It counts it, says why on the recording, and logs a gap. A file never mixes data of different quality.
- It starts **by itself** if you want: "every trading day, record NIFTY and BANKNIFTY option chains, ATM plus or minus 10, current weekly expiry, every 30 seconds, during market hours". Auto-record is **off until you turn it on**.
- It stays out of your way: it reads from the live feed first, then from the cache, and only then asks the broker, at the lowest priority and inside a share cap (see [Saving API calls](#saving-api-calls)).
- It stops writing before a disk limit is passed, and tells you first.

## Start in one minute

Open the dashboard, Data, Recordings, and press **Record index option chains**. Or from a terminal:

```
mc-bridge record preset index-option-chains     # adds the rule and turns auto-record on
mc-bridge record status                         # Recording today: 2 rules, 86 symbols, 38 KB, last write 12:29:44.
```

A manual recording, for example a price a second for two symbols:

```
mc-bridge record quotes NSE:NIFTY NSE:RELIANCE --every 1
mc-bridge record chain NIFTY --every 30 --expiry 2026-11-17 --strikes 10
mc-bridge record list
mc-bridge record show <id>
mc-bridge record stop <id>
```

The commands need an admin key (`--key`, or `MCB_ADMIN_KEY` in the environment) and the Bridge running on this computer.

## What is recorded

| Kind | What you give | What is saved | How often |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quotes` | symbols, a collection, or an underlying with a universe | price, bid, ask, quantities, volume, open interest, day open/high/low/close | `everySec`, at least 1 (from the live feed). Symbols the feed does not carry are read from the broker, which needs 5 seconds or more |
| `chain` | an underlying (with expiry and strikes), a collection, or option symbols | every leg of the chain: price, bid, ask, open interest and its change, volume, IV and Greeks when known, the spot price | `everySec`, at least 15 |

Strikes, expiries and the ATM are chosen like this:

- `expiries`: `current-weekly`, `next-weekly`, `current-monthly`, `all-weekly` (the next five weeks), or a list of dates. The expiry rolls on its own: the rule is worked out again each trading day.
- `strikes`: `{ "around": "atm", "count": 10 }` or `{ "from": 23000, "to": 25000 }`. The ATM comes from the real-time price and moves during the day. The window is looked at again every 30 minutes (`recorder.reResolveMinutes`); symbols are added, never dropped, so the day's files do not lose a strike when the price drifts.
- **No guessing.** If the price is delayed, stale or missing, the ATM window is not built from it. The recording waits, says why in its status, logs a gap "The symbols to record could not be chosen", and tries again every minute.
- A **collection** (from the library) is resolved again every day by the library. A resolution that rests on a delayed or end-of-day price is refused the same way.

## Market hours

By default a recording runs only inside the exchange session of each trading day. That comes from the Bridge's market calendar (holidays, weekends, special sessions such as Muhurat). For NSE, BSE, NFO and BFO it opens at the open and stops at the close by itself. Your own days and hours work too (IST, trading days only):

```
mc-bridge record rule add chain NIFTY --every 30 --days mon,tue,wed --start 09:30 --end 14:00
```

MCX and CDS have their own hours that the calendar does not hold. For them use `--all-day` or an explicit schedule. All-day recordings roll to a new file at IST midnight.

The calendar is a dated list, not a live feed from the exchange; the market calendar answers say when a holiday row is not verified. If the Bridge thinks a day is a holiday and it is not, check the exchange's circular and tell the Bridge with a custom schedule.

## Auto-record rules

A rule is "what to record, how often, when". Rules live in `recordings/rules.json` in the data folder, or in `recorder.autoRecord.rules` in the config file (those are read-only through the API).

```
POST /v1/recordings/rules
{
  "name": "Index option chains",
  "kind": "chain",
  "underlying": ["NIFTY", "BANKNIFTY"],
  "universe": { "expiries": "current-weekly", "strikes": { "around": "atm", "count": 10 }, "sides": ["CE", "PE"], "includeUnderlying": true },
  "everySec": 30,
  "schedule": "market-hours",
  "keepDays": 60
}
```

Rule fields: `id`, `name`, `enabled`, `kind`, one of `symbols` / `collection` / `underlying` (+ `universe`), `everySec`, `schedule` (`"market-hours"` or `{ days, start, end }`), `keepDays`, `maxDiskMb`, `compress`, `format`.

What the Bridge does with them, by itself:

1. At the session start it starts the rule's recording (bus event `recording.started`), chooses the symbols and subscribes them to the live feed.
2. At the session end it stops (`recording.stopped`, reason `session-end`).
3. The next trading day it chooses the symbols again: the expiry rolls, the ATM follows the price.
4. After a restart it picks up where it was. The time the Bridge was off is logged as a gap.
5. **No login at the session start?** It sends `account.login_needed` once that day (so the morning reminder and Telegram can tell you), logs a "login missing" gap, and starts writing as soon as a login or a feed is available.

Turn rules on and off with `mc-bridge record auto on|off`, `PUT /v1/recordings/auto`, or the dashboard. Turning auto-record off stops every rule's recording; the files stay.

### Presets

| Preset | What it adds |
|---|---|
| `index-option-chains` | NIFTY and BANKNIFTY chains, ATM plus or minus 10, current expiry, every 30 s, market hours |
| `my-watchlist` | every symbol of the collection `watchlist` (or another one: `--collection name`), one price a second from the live feed, market hours. Needs the library of collections |

Applying a preset creates its rule and turns auto-record on. Applying it again does not add a second copy.

## Status in plain words

`GET /v1/recordings/status`, `mc-bridge record status` and the dashboard show one line:

```
Recording today: 3 rules, 41 symbols, 18 MB, last write 09:31:02.
```

or what is wrong: `Auto-record is on: 3 recordings waiting for 10 Nov 09:15 IST.`, `; 1 gap today (one is open now)`, `; writing stopped on a disk limit`. Each recording has its own sentence (`statusText`), its counters, its gaps and its disk use.

## Gaps

A gap is a stretch inside a session when nothing was saved. Each one has a start, an end and a reason:

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `login-missing` | no broker account was logged in |
| `feed-down` | the live feed was down and the broker could not be read instead |
| `feed-silent` | the feed sent nothing |
| `budget` | the broker's budget was in use by other work, or the broker asked the Bridge to slow down |
| `delayed-source` | the only data was delayed or end-of-day, which is never recorded |
| `universe-unresolved` | the symbols could not be chosen honestly (see above) |
| `bridge-stopped` | the Bridge was not running |
| `disk-full` | a disk limit was reached |

A gap opens after silence of `recorder.gapAfterSec` (default three intervals, at least 30 seconds), except login-missing and disk-full, which open at once. They are kept in `gaps.jsonl` in the recording's folder, shown in `GET /v1/recordings/{recordingId}`, and sent as `recording.gap` events (`state` open, then closed). A quiet symbol that simply has not traded is not a gap: the feed is alive.

## Files

Everything is under the data folder, `recordings/<id>/`, where `<id>` is `rec_xxxxxxxx` for a manual recording and `rule-<ruleId>` for a rule. One file per symbol per IST trading day:

```
recordings/rule-index-option-chains/2026-11-09__NFO_NIFTY-2026-11-09-24000-CE.csv
recordings/rule-index-option-chains/2026-11-09__NSE_NIFTY.csv
recordings/rule-index-option-chains/2026-11-06__NSE_NIFTY.csv.gz       (a finished day, compressed)
recordings/rule-index-option-chains/recording.json                    what it is
recordings/rule-index-option-chains/state.json, index.json            counters and row counts (rebuilt if lost)
recordings/rule-index-option-chains/gaps.jsonl                        the gaps
```

The file name is `<YYYY-MM-DD>__<symbol with : written as _>.<csv|jsonl>[.gz]`. The date is the IST day the rows were sampled. Files are created readable by your user only.

Columns (CSV; JSON lines use the same names). Empty means "not known":

`time, symbol, ltp, bid, ask, bidQty, askQty, volume, oi, oiChange, open, high, low, close, iv, delta, gamma, theta, vega, spot, tickAt, source, class`

- `time`: when the sample was taken, ISO with `+05:30`.
- `tickAt`: when the price itself was last updated. A quiet symbol shows an older `tickAt` than `time`; nothing is hidden.
- `source`: `stream` (the live feed), `cache` or `broker`.
- `class`: always `realtime`.
- `spot`: the underlying's price in the chain snapshot. `iv` is in percent.

List and download files through the API (`GET /v1/recordings/{recordingId}/files`, `.../files/{name}`), the dashboard, or just open them in Excel or Python. A crash can leave the last line unfinished; the next write starts on a fresh line and readers skip the torn one.

### Reading them back

Anything that reads local data (history, downloads, datasets) can use `server/bridge/recorder/reader.mjs`:

```js
import { readRecorded } from "./recorder/reader.mjs";
const { rows, gaps, recordings } = readRecorded({ dataDir, symbol: "NSE:NIFTY", fromMs, toMs });
```

It reads plain and `.gz` files, orders the rows by time and returns the gaps inside the range, so the caller can ask the broker only for the gaps and the missing tail. Pandas: `pd.read_csv(path)` (or `read_json(path, lines=True)`).

## Disk safety and retention

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `recorder.maxDiskMb` | 5000 | all recordings together |
| a recording's or rule's `maxDiskMb` | none | that recording only |
| `recorder.minFreeDiskMb` | 500 | stop when the disk has less free than this |
| `recorder.retentionDays` / `keepDays` | none | keep this many days of files (today included); older day files are deleted |
| `recorder.compressFinished` / `compress` | off | gzip the files of finished days |

At 90 % of a limit (and when free space is below twice the floor) the Bridge sends `recording.disk_low` with `level: "warning"`, once a day per limit. At the limit it **stops writing before passing it**: the sample that would not fit is dropped whole, the recording shows `blocked` with the reason, a gap `disk-full` opens and `recording.disk_low` is sent with `level: "stopped"`. It starts again when there is room (retention ran, you deleted something). Day files are tidied at start, at the first pass of each new day and every hour.

## Saving API calls

- **The live feed first.** Quotes and chain legs that the feed carries cost no broker call. The recorder subscribes the symbols it records (up to `recorder.maxStreamSymbols`, 400 per recording). Calls avoided are counted in the scheduler's savings and shown as `apiCalls.savedToday`.
- **Background priority, share cap.** When it does need the broker, a recording asks at the lowest ("background") priority and may use at most `recorder.maxBudgetShare` (default 0.3, never above 0.5) of an account's spare budget. A live read, an order check or another key always goes first. If the broker asks the Bridge to slow down, broker reads pause for the time it names and the recording uses the live feed only; the missed samples are logged as a `budget` gap.
- **One chain call per expiry.** All the legs of an expiry come from one chain read, however many strikes you record.
- A chain recording never asks for data from a backup source (`allowBackup` is off): those are delayed or unofficial and never recorded.

## Settings

```json
"recorder": {
  "enabled": true,
  "maxRecordings": 10,
  "maxDiskMb": 5000,
  "retentionDays": null,
  "compressFinished": false,
  "minFreeDiskMb": 500,
  "maxBudgetShare": 0.3,
  "maxSymbolsPerRecording": 1000,
  "maxStreamSymbols": 400,
  "gapAfterSec": null,
  "reResolveMinutes": 30,
  "autoRecord": { "enabled": false, "rules": [] }
}
```

`maxRecordings` counts running, paused and waiting recordings, rules included.

## Routes and events

Reading needs a `read` key. Starting, changing or deleting a recording or a rule needs an admin key used from this computer (it uses this computer's disk and your broker's budget).

| Route | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/recordings`, `POST /v1/recordings` | list, start a manual recording |
| `GET /v1/recordings/status` | the plain line and numbers |
| `GET /v1/recordings/{recordingId}`, `DELETE`, `POST .../pause`, `.../resume`, `.../stop` | one recording |
| `GET /v1/recordings/{recordingId}/files`, `.../files/{name}` | the day files |
| `GET/PUT /v1/recordings/auto` | the auto-record switch |
| `GET/POST /v1/recordings/rules`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/recordings/rules/{ruleId}` | rules |
| `GET /v1/recordings/presets`, `POST .../presets/{preset}/apply` | presets |

A recording that belongs to a rule is changed through the rule. Deleting a rule keeps its files unless you add `?deleteFiles=true`.

Bus topics (also in the notifications and event streams): `recording.started`, `recording.stopped`, `recording.gap`, `recording.disk_low`.

## Questions

**Why is a recording "waiting"?** Outside the session, on a holiday, or no login yet. Its sentence says which, and when it starts next.

**Can I record when the Bridge is off?** No. It records only while it runs. Run it on a computer that is on during market hours, or see [vps.md](vps.md).

**Why nothing for an illiquid option?** If it did not trade, there is no new price. Its rows carry the time of its last price (`tickAt`). Chains give a price per leg at each snapshot.

**Is this advice or analysis?** No. It saves data. What you do with it is your own work.

---

<!-- docs/guides/amibroker.md -->

# AmiBroker

Everything AmiBroker can reach is read-only: `/xl/*` cannot place orders. Full instructions and the files:
[integrations/amibroker](../../integrations/amibroker/README.md).

## Live values in AFL

1. Copy `integrations/amibroker/mrchartist-bridge.afl` into AmiBroker's `Formulas\Include` folder.
2. Create a read-only URL key (AmiBroker cannot send headers):
   `mc-bridge keys create --label amibroker --scope read --allow-query`
3. Store it outside your formulas: the Windows user variable `MCB_AMIBROKER_KEY` (restart AmiBroker), or the only line
   of `%USERPROFILE%\.mc-bridge\amibroker.key`.
4. Use it:

```c
#include_once <mrchartist-bridge.afl>

nifty = McbLtp("NSE:NIFTY");
oi    = McbQuote("NFO:NIFTY-2026-10-27-FUT", "oi");
chg   = McbQuote("NSE:RELIANCE", "changePct");

Title = StrFormat("NIFTY %.2f   FUT OI %.0f   RELIANCE %.2f%%", nifty, oi, chg);
```

Each value is fetched at most once per `McbMinIntervalMs` (1 s by default) per symbol, and the Bridge answers from
its stream or cache first, so a chart refreshing many times a second does not multiply broker calls. Fields:
`ltp, open, high, low, close, change, changePct, volume, oi, bid, ask`. Set `MCB_BRIDGE_URL` if the Bridge is not on
`http://127.0.0.1:4300`.

## History via ASCII import

```powershell
$h = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:MCB_AMIBROKER_KEY" }
Invoke-WebRequest -Headers $h -OutFile nifty-5m.csv `
  "http://127.0.0.1:4300/xl/history?symbol=NSE:NIFTY&interval=5m&countback=2000&layout=amibroker"
```

Import with *File → Import ASCII* and the shipped `mrchartist-intraday.format` (or `mrchartist-eod.format` for daily
and longer). Times are IST bar-open times.
