<!-- docs/guides/developers.md -->

# Building on the Bridge: the developer guide

This is the short path for someone who writes code against the Bridge: a working call in five minutes, which key to
use, what to do when something fails, and what will not change under you. Everything here also lives in the dashboard
on the **Developers** page (`#/developers`): apps, a scope finder, your requests live and every error explained.

## Start in five minutes

1. Start the Bridge. For sample data and no broker: `mc-bridge start --demo`. Its address is `http://127.0.0.1:4300`
   unless you changed it. Check it answers (no key needed): `curl http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/health`.
2. Make a project with the address and a key already in it:

   ```bash
   mc-bridge init node --with-key        # or: python, curl, sheets, webhook-receiver, mcp-client
   cd bridge-node && node index.mjs
   ```

   `mc-bridge init --list` shows the starters. Each one writes a new folder with a README that has three runnable steps.
   `--with-key` makes one key with only the `read` scope (or `--scope paper`), an expiry (90 days by default,
   `--expires 30d` to change it) and writes it **only** to `.env`, which `.gitignore` lists. The key is never printed.
   Without `--with-key` no key is made and the README says how.
3. Or by hand: open the dashboard, **Developers > Create app**, pick what it is for, copy the key (it is shown once)
   and run the curl line.

The starters use nothing but Node 22, Python 3.9 or `curl`. They are tested against a demo Bridge, and the calls to newer
features (downloads, events) say plainly "this Bridge does not have it yet" on an older Bridge instead of failing.

## Auth and scopes

Every call except `GET /v1/health` and `GET /openapi.yaml` needs `Authorization: Bearer mcb_<id>_<secret>`. Never put a
key in a web address; the one exception is `?key=` on the read-only `/xl/*` routes for tools that cannot send headers.

| Scope | May | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | prices, history, option chains, positions, funds | scripts, charts, spreadsheets, AI assistants |
| `paper` | everything `read` does, plus paper orders | a bot that tries ideas |
| `live` | real orders, when every live opt-in is on | made on purpose with `mc-bridge keys create` |
| `admin` | keys, quotas, settings; this computer only | tools you run yourself |

A route's scope is in the OpenAPI file (`x-scope`) and on its page under `docs/api/`. The dashboard's scope finder (Developers >
Apps) answers "which key does this call need?" from this Bridge's own routes. A key can never grant more than it holds, an
assistant key (`--client mcp`) can never be an admin key, and approving an order always stays on this computer.

An **app** is just a key with a name, its scope, expiry, quota and use (last used, requests today). The Apps view reads
`/v1/keys` and `/v1/quotas`; there is no separate store. Revoke an app and it stops on its very next request.

## Limits and retries

Every key has its own rate and daily cap, and all keys share each broker's real limits. A refusal is HTTP `429` with
`Retry-After` (whole seconds) and, in the body, `scope` (whose limit it was), `retryAfterMs` and `limit`. Wait that long, then
retry; do not retry in a tight loop. The starters do this for you: a read is retried up to three times, waiting as long as the
Bridge says. See [rate-limits.md](rate-limits.md) for how the budget is shared.

Retry only what is safe. A read can always be repeated. A write can be repeated only with an idempotency key (below), and
`OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` is never retried blindly: check the order book first. Every error has a `retryable` flag that says which is which.

## Errors

Every error is `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`, `status`, `detail`, `retryable` and `requestId`. Switch on
`code`, never on `detail`. The full list, with what each means and what to do, is in the dashboard (Developers > Errors),
at `GET /v1/errors` (the list of this Bridge's own codes) and in [the error codes page](../api/errors.md). A test fails when a
code has no entry there. When you report a problem, quote the `requestId`.

## Pagination

List routes take `limit` and an opaque `cursor`; the answer's `meta.nextCursor` is the cursor for the next page and is `null`
on the last one. Do not build or read a cursor.

## Idempotency

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (any unique string, for example a UUID) with every order write. A repeat with the same key and
the same body returns the first result (the answer has `Idempotency-Replayed: true`); the same key with a different body is
`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; while the first is still running you get `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`, which is safe to retry.

## Events

Instead of polling, react to Bridge events. Everything stays on your computer: the Bridge keeps the last events on disk and
sends signed requests only to addresses you give it.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/events/stream` | Server-sent events. `?topics=order.*,download.done` filters (a topic, a prefix such as `order.*`, or `*`); `?since=<cursor>` or the `Last-Event-ID` header replays what you missed after a reconnect |
| `GET /v1/events`, `GET /v1/events/topics` | Recent events as a list, and the topics that exist |
| `/v1/subscriptions`, `/v1/subscriptions/{id}` | Signed outbound webhooks (create, list, change, delete) |
| `POST /v1/subscriptions/{id}/test`, `GET /v1/subscriptions/{id}/deliveries` | Send a test event; see the delivery log |

A webhook request carries the event as JSON and these headers: `X-Bridge-Signature`, `X-Bridge-Timestamp`, `X-Bridge-Event-Id`,
`X-Bridge-Delivery` and `X-Bridge-Attempt`. The signature is

```text
X-Bridge-Timestamp: <unix seconds>
X-Bridge-Signature: v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>." + the exact raw body)>
```

Verify it before you trust the body: sign the raw bytes (never re-serialised JSON), compare in constant time, reject a timestamp
more than 300 seconds off, and remember `X-Bridge-Event-Id` so a retry is handled once (delivery is at least once). In Node:

```js
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
function verify({ secret, timestamp, signature, rawBody, toleranceSec = 300 }) {
  if (!timestamp || !signature || !/^\d{1,12}$/.test(timestamp)) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(timestamp)) > toleranceSec) return false;
  const want = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${timestamp}.`).update(rawBody).digest();
  // the header may hold several signatures ("v1=aaa v1=bbb") while a secret is being replaced
  return signature.split(/[\s,]+/).some((part) => {
    const m = /^v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$/i.exec(part);
    return m !== null && timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(m[1], "hex"), want);
  });
}
```

and in Python:

```python
import hashlib, hmac, re, time
def verify(secret: str, timestamp: str, signature: str, raw: bytes, tolerance=300) -> bool:
    if not timestamp or not signature or not re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,12}", timestamp):
        return False
    if abs(time.time() - int(timestamp)) > tolerance:
        return False
    want = hmac.new(secret.encode(), timestamp.encode() + b"." + raw, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return any(m and hmac.compare_digest(m.group(1).lower(), want) for m in (re.fullmatch(r"v1=([0-9a-fA-F]{64})", p) for p in re.split(r"[\s,]+", signature)))
```

With curl and openssl you can sign a test body: `printf '%s' "$T.$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SECRET"`.
The `webhook-receiver` starter is a complete receiver that does all of this. Creating a subscription needs an admin key and works
from this computer only, because the target is an address the Bridge will call. By default only `https` targets are allowed; a
receiver on this computer (`http://127.0.0.1:...`) needs `events.webhooks.allowPrivateTargets: true` in the Bridge's config file,
which cannot be switched on over HTTP. The signing secret must be 16 to 256 characters and is write-only: the Bridge never shows
it again.

## Data downloads

`POST /v1/downloads` saves history to files on the Bridge's computer (a job you can watch, pause and resume); `GET /v1/datasets`
lists the data sets that update only what is new. Every file says its data class (`realtime`, `delayed` or `eod`), its source and
its delay, and data that is not realtime never feeds orders, risk checks, paper fills or alerts. The Node, Python and curl starters
each have a `download` example that works when the Bridge has the feature and says so when it does not.

## The versioning promise

Routes under `/v1` only gain things. A field is not renamed or removed, a route is not removed, an error `code` is never renamed,
and a scope never grows silently. A change that would break a program gets a new version beside the old one (`/v2`), and the old
one keeps working for a long, announced time. New optional fields and new error codes can appear at any time, so ignore fields you
do not know and treat an unknown `code` by its `status` and `retryable`. The OpenAPI file served at `/openapi.yaml` is the contract.

## Where next

- [quickstart.md](quickstart.md): the same five minutes with a paper order and a stream.
- [python.md](python.md) and [typescript.md](typescript.md): the fuller clients in `sdk/`.
- [../api/README.md](../api/README.md): one page per call, with curl and Python.
- [../collections/README.md](../collections/README.md): Postman and Bruno collections.
- [mcp.md](mcp.md): AI assistants.

<!-- docs/guides/python.md -->

# Python

The Python library uses the standard library only (Python 3.9+): HTTP, a small WebSocket client and an asyncio client are
built in. It is typed (`py.typed`), pleasant in notebooks, and safe by default: orders are paper unless you say
`live=True`, and delayed data cannot feed an order. Full reference: [sdk/python/README.md](../../sdk/python/README.md).

```bash
pip install ./sdk/python                      # add the pandas extra for DataFrames: pip install "./sdk/python[pandas]"
mc-bridge keys create --label py --scope read,paper    # shown once; copy it
python -m mrchartist_bridge login             # saves the URL and key for this user (owner-only file), then pings
```

Or set `MCB_API_KEY` (and `MCB_BRIDGE_URL` when the Bridge is not at `http://127.0.0.1:4300`). Use a read or paper key for
scripts; a key that can trade live or administer the Bridge does not belong in a notebook or a spreadsheet.

## Connect

```python
from mrchartist_bridge import Bridge

bridge = Bridge()            # URL and key found from arguments, MCB_*, the Bridge's config and client.json
print(bridge.ping())         # is it up, how fast, is the key accepted
demo = Bridge.demo()         # the same, but only if the Bridge is in demo mode (sample prices, paper only)
```

Where the URL and key come from, in order, is in `mrchartist_bridge/discovery.py`. The library never reads the Bridge's data
folder or its control token. A missing key, a wrong key, a Bridge that is not running and a key without the needed scope each
raise a typed error with a one-line fix.

## Market data and freshness

```python
quotes = bridge.quotes(["NSE:NIFTY", "NSE:RELIANCE"])         # a list of Quote; quotes.errors holds symbols that failed
for q in quotes:
    f = q.freshness
    print(q.symbol, q.ltp, f.source, f.data_class, f.delay_sec, f.official, f.confidence, f.flags)

q = bridge.quote("NSE:RELIANCE")
q.require_realtime()          # NotRealtime for delayed, end-of-day, unofficial or stale data
```

Real-time data comes from your own broker accounts. Free sources and plugins answer with `class` `delayed` or `eod` and are
fine for charts and analysis, never for orders, risk checks, paper fills or alerts (see [sources](sources.md)).
`history.freshness`, `depth.freshness` and every `Ltp` carry the same label.

## Orders

```python
from mrchartist_bridge import NotRealtime, OrderRefused, OutcomeUnknown

try:
    order = bridge.orders.place("NFO:NIFTY-2026-12-29-FUT", "BUY", lots=1, product="MARGIN", price=bridge.quote("NFO:NIFTY-2026-12-29-FUT"))
    done = bridge.orders.wait_for_fill(order, timeout=30)
except NotRealtime as e:        # the quote was delayed or stale: nothing was sent
    ...
except OrderRefused as e:       # kill switch, market closed, paper only, invalid order ...: e.code says which
    ...
except OutcomeUnknown as e:     # the Bridge cannot tell if the broker took it: use e.idempotency_key and e.client_order_id
    ...
```

- `place` sends `mode="paper"`; live needs `live=True` and everything the Bridge requires for live trading (see [safety](safety.md)).
- Every write has an `Idempotency-Key` and a generated client order id. Calling again with the same two ids returns the first
  order with `replayed=True`.
- An unknown outcome is looked up by client order id. You get the order back, or `OutcomeUnknown`; the library never sends a
  second order for you.
- `orders.preview(...)`, `orders.cancel(...)`, `orders.modify(...)`, `orders.list(...)`, `orders.to_target(...)` and
  `orders.batch(...)` follow the same rules. `to_target` and `batch` use `POST /v1/orders/to-target` and
  `POST /v1/orders/batch` on a Bridge that has them and fall back to the library otherwise; an unreadable position is
  `PositionUnknown`, never treated as flat.
- Orders that need a person (AI assistants, hooks that ask for confirmation) wait as tickets. `bridge.tickets.wait(id)` reports
  `confirmed`, `rejected` or `expired`. Approval itself stays on the Bridge's computer, in the dashboard: there is no call in the
  library that confirms a ticket.

## Streams

```python
with bridge.stream(["NSE:NIFTY", "NSE:RELIANCE"], mode="quote", orders=True) as s:
    for event in s.events():                  # Tick, Snapshot, OrderUpdate, FeedStatus, Heartbeat, GoAway ...
        print(event)
print(s.gaps, s.conflated, s.reconnects)
```

The stream reconnects with a fresh single-use token, re-subscribes everything, waits as `go_away` asks, and counts `seq` gaps
and conflated ticks (a slow reader skips values; the newest always arrives). `s.on("tick", fn).run()` is the callback form.
For asyncio: `async with AsyncBridge().stream([...]) as s: async for event in s.events(): ...`.

## asyncio

```python
async with AsyncBridge() as bridge:
    nifty, bank = await asyncio.gather(bridge.price("NSE:NIFTY"), bridge.price("NSE:BANKNIFTY"))
    order = await bridge.orders.place("NSE:RELIANCE", "BUY", quantity=1, product="CNC", price=nifty)
```

`AsyncBridge` runs the blocking calls in worker threads (up to `max_concurrency`, default 8). For many symbols use
`await bridge.ltp_many(symbols)`.

## pandas, CSV and spreadsheets

```python
df = bridge.history("NSE:RELIANCE", "1d", countback=250).to_dataframe()   # IST index, freshness columns
bridge.quotes(symbols).to_dataframe()
from mrchartist_bridge import frames
frames.to_csv(bridge.history("NSE:RELIANCE", "5m", countback=300), "reliance.csv")
print(bridge.xl.formula("ltp"))                                          # an Excel =WEBSERVICE(...) formula, key left as a placeholder
```

## Downloads, datasets and recordings

The Bridge can fetch history for many symbols in the background and keep it as files, and can record what brokers do not
give you (option chains, open-interest snapshots) going forward from its own live data. The library drives both.

```python
job = bridge.downloads.create(["NSE:RELIANCE", "NSE:TCS"], "5m", from_="2024-01-01", dataset="large-caps-5m")
job = bridge.downloads.wait(job, on_progress=lambda j: print(j.status, j.progress.done, "of", j.progress.total))
bridge.downloads.save(job, "data/")          # checks each file's SHA-256, writes manifest.json, skips files already there
rows = bridge.downloads.read(job)            # list of dicts (as_dataframe=True for pandas)
bridge.datasets.update("large-caps-5m", wait=True)      # later: only the bars after the last stored one
```

- A job runs at the lowest priority on the Bridge, so it never slows live reads or orders, survives a restart, and stops with
  a stated reason (`job.reason`) on a kill switch or a lost login. `wait` raises `DownloadFailed` with that reason, or
  `WaitTimeout` (the job carries on; look again with `downloads.get(id)`).
- Every job, dataset and recording says its data class, source and delay (`job.data_class`, `job.label`) and `save()` keeps
  that in `manifest.json`. `backup=True` lets a free source serve a job; its files are then `delayed` or `eod`, for analysis
  only, never for orders, risk checks, paper fills or alerts.
- `bridge.recordings.create("chain", underlying="NIFTY", expiry="2026-11-12", every_sec=30)` records chains (at least 15 s
  apart) and `create("quotes", symbols, every_sec=1)` quotes. The Bridge records real-time data only. For recording without
  pressing start, `bridge.recordings.rules.create("Index chains", "chain", every_sec=30, collection="index-options")`: the Bridge
  starts and stops it at each trading session, resumes after a restart and notes a gap when the feed was missing.
- A collection is a named, tagged list that downloads, recordings and sheets share: `bridge.collections.create("w", symbols)`
  or `create("nifty-near", universe=option_universe("NIFTY", "current-weekly", count=10))`. `resolve(name)` gives the symbols
  now; for an option universe it recomputes the ATM and the rolling expiry each time and puts a note in `warnings` when
  the price was stale. The Bridge refuses an ATM from a delayed or end-of-day price (422) and from a stale one (503) unless you
  pass `allow_stale=True`, and then labels the answer (`warnings`, `atm_source`). Reading collections needs a `read` key; changing
  them needs the `paper` scope. `export`/`import_` move a collection as CSV or JSON.

## Candles over any range, and saving API calls

```python
candles = bridge.history_all("NSE:RELIANCE", "5m", "2024-01-01", "2024-12-31", local_first=True)
for c in candles:                  # typed Candle objects, oldest first, no duplicates
    ...
df = candles.to_dataframe()        # also .records(), .to_csv(path), .to_history(); freshness columns stay on
print(candles.freshness, candles.local_windows, candles.broker_windows, candles.gaps)
```

One `GET /v1/history` call covers only so much; `history_all` asks for windows that fit (and halves any the Bridge reports as
`partial`). With `local_first=True` the Bridge answers from data it already stored (real-time class, no gaps) and asks the
broker only for what is missing; `local_windows` and `broker_windows` show the split. Parquet is written only when `pyarrow`
is installed: `candles.to_parquet("x.parquet")` or `frames.csv_to_parquet("x.csv")` (the label goes in the file metadata).

## Events and webhooks

```python
for ev in bridge.events.subscribe(["download.*", "recording.gap"], since=saved_cursor):
    print(ev.cursor, ev.topic, ev.data)       # reconnects by itself; asks for events after the last cursor
```

`subscribe` reads `GET /v1/events/stream`, reconnects with growing waits and resumes from the last cursor, so a restart loses
nothing the Bridge still keeps. If the cursor you ask for is older than what the Bridge kept (or newer than it has), `sub.gap`
is true (`sub.gap_reason` is `retention` or `cursor_ahead`; `sub.on_gap` is called): read the current state from the API
again, then carry on. `bridge.events.poll(since=cursor)` is the same as one JSON answer for a script that runs now and then, and
`bridge.events.topics()` lists what your key may receive.

For a URL on your own server use `bridge.subscriptions.create(url, topics, secret=...)` (admin key, from the Bridge's
computer) and check every delivery before you trust it:

```python
from mrchartist_bridge import verify_signature
ok = verify_signature(SECRET, raw_body_bytes, request.headers)        # False: answer 401 and do not process it
```

The Bridge sends `X-Bridge-Signature: v1=<hex>` and `X-Bridge-Timestamp: <unix seconds>` (and `X-Bridge-Event-Id`,
`X-Bridge-Delivery`, `X-Bridge-Attempt`). The hex is the HMAC-SHA256 of `"<timestamp>." + the exact raw body`; a timestamp more
than 5 minutes off fails. Use the raw bytes as received. Delivery is at least once: de-duplicate on `X-Bridge-Event-Id`.
`raise_on_fail=True` raises `SignatureInvalid` with a `reason`. A delivery that keeps failing becomes a dead letter:
`bridge.subscriptions.dead_letters(id)`, `retry_dead_letter(id, letter)`, `retry_all_dead_letters(id)`, `clear_dead_letters(id)`;
`deliveries(id, outcome="dead")` is the attempt log.

## Rate limits and many symbols

`bridge.ltp_many(symbols)` and `quotes_many` split into requests the Bridge accepts and wait when throttled.
`mrchartist_bridge.batching.retry(fn)` retries a read honouring `Retry-After` and the refusal's `scope`
(`client`, `upstream`, `queue`, `consumer-cap`); it never retries an unknown order outcome.

## Alerts

`mrchartist_bridge.alerts` builds and checks the JSON an alert sends to a hook (`AlertMessage`), signs it for `generic` hooks
(`alerts.sign`), and sends it (`alerts.send`: a real alert, so a paper hook places a paper order). `bridge.hooks.test(...)` and
`bridge.hooks.signals(...)` use routes that newer Bridges add and raise `FeatureUnavailable` on older ones. This module follows
[alerts](webhooks.md) and is marked provisional until the message format is final.

## The original client and strategies

`BridgeClient` (one method per route, plain dicts, the Bridge's `{data, meta, errors}` envelope) is unchanged and is
`bridge.client`. `mrchartist_bridge.strategy` is kept as it was (`python -m mrchartist_bridge strategy run file.py`).
Tests: `python -m pytest sdk/python/tests -q`.

---

<!-- docs/guides/typescript.md -->

# TypeScript and Node

A small client with no runtime dependencies (Node 20+), with TypeScript types in `src/index.d.ts`. Streaming uses
Node 22's built-in `WebSocket` or the `ws` package. Full method list: [sdk/node/README.md](../../sdk/node/README.md).

```bash
npm install /path/to/api-bridge-v2/sdk/node      # or: npm install ws  (Node 20/21 streaming)
```

```ts
import { BridgeClient, BridgeApiError } from "@mrchartist/bridge-client";

const bridge = new BridgeClient({ apiKey: process.env.MCB_API_KEY! });   // baseUrl defaults to http://127.0.0.1:4300

const { data, errors } = await bridge.quotes(["NSE:NIFTY", "NSE:RELIANCE"]);
for (const q of data) console.log(q.symbol, q.ltp, q.freshness.source, q.freshness.ageMs);

try {
  const { data: order, replayed, idempotencyKey } = await bridge.placeOrder({
    account: "paper", symbol: "NSE:RELIANCE", side: "BUY", quantity: 1, product: "CNC", orderType: "MARKET",
  });
  console.log(order.orderId, order.status, replayed, idempotencyKey);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof BridgeApiError) console.error(e.status, e.code, e.detail);
  else throw e;
}

const stream = bridge.stream({ symbols: ["NSE:NIFTY"], mode: "ltp", orders: true });
stream.on("tick", (t) => console.log(t.symbol, t.ltp));
stream.on("order", (m) => console.log(m.order.status));
```

Same guarantees as the Python client: an `Idempotency-Key` on every order write, retries only where the Bridge says
an error is retryable, never a blind retry of a write (`BridgeConnectionError` with `outcomeUnknown: true`), the key
sent only as a header, and single-use stream tokens.

## Downloads, recordings, collections, history and events

The Bridge can fetch history for many symbols in the background and keep it as files, record option chains and quotes going
forward from its own live data, keep named lists of instruments, and tell you what happened without polling. These groups
return the reply's `data`; the plain one-route-one-method calls (`createDownload`, `listCollections`, ...) return the envelope.

```ts
import { BridgeClient, optionUniverse, verifySignature, DownloadFailedError } from "@mrchartist/bridge-client";

let job = await bridge.downloads.create({ symbols: ["NSE:RELIANCE", "NSE:TCS"], intervals: "5m", from: "2024-01-01", dataset: "large-caps-5m" });
try {
  job = await bridge.downloads.wait(job, { onProgress: (j) => console.log(j.status, j.progress.done, "of", j.progress.total) });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof DownloadFailedError) console.error(e.job.reason);   // kill switch, lost login, full disk ...
  else throw e;
}
await bridge.downloads.save(job, "data/");      // each file checked against its SHA-256; manifest.json (with the data class) written
await bridge.datasets.update("large-caps-5m", { wait: true });   // later: only the bars after the last stored one

await bridge.recordings.rules.create({ name: "Index chains", kind: "chain", everySec: 30, collection: "index-options" });
await bridge.collections.create("nifty-near", { universe: optionUniverse({ underlying: "NIFTY", count: 10 }) });
const { symbols, warnings } = await bridge.collections.resolve("nifty-near");   // refused (422/503) on a delayed or stale price unless { allowStale: true }; then warnings say so

for await (const c of bridge.historyAll({ symbol: "NSE:RELIANCE", interval: "5m", from: "2024-01-01", localFirst: true })) { /* typed Candle */ }
for await (const ev of bridge.events.subscribe({ topics: ["download.*"], since: savedCursor })) console.log(ev.cursor, ev.topic, ev.data);
```

- Jobs run at the lowest priority on the Bridge (they never slow live reads or orders), survive a restart and stop with a stated
  reason. Every job, dataset and recording says its data class, source and delay; delayed and end-of-day files are for analysis
  only, never for orders, risk checks, paper fills or alerts.
- `historyAll` asks for windows that fit the Bridge's per-call limit and halves any it reports as `partial`. With
  `localFirst: true` the Bridge answers from data it already stored (real-time class, no gaps) and asks the broker only for the
  rest: `candles.localWindows` and `candles.brokerWindows` show the split, and `candles.freshness` is the least current label.
- `events.subscribe` reconnects with growing waits and resumes after the last cursor, so a restart loses nothing the Bridge
  still keeps. For a URL on your side, `bridge.subscriptions.create({ url, topics, secret })` (admin key, from the Bridge's
  computer) and check every delivery on the raw body: `verifySignature(secret, rawBody, req.headers)`. The Bridge sends
  `X-Bridge-Signature: v1=<hex>` and `X-Bridge-Timestamp: <unix seconds>` (plus `X-Bridge-Event-Id`, `X-Bridge-Delivery`,
  `X-Bridge-Attempt`); the hex is the HMAC-SHA256 of `"<timestamp>." + raw body`, with a 5-minute window. Delivery is at least
  once: de-duplicate on `X-Bridge-Event-Id`. A delivery that keeps failing becomes a dead letter:
  `bridge.subscriptions.deadLetters(id)`, `retryDeadLetter`, `retryAllDeadLetters`, `clearDeadLetters`.
- If the cursor you pass is older than what the Bridge kept, `sub.gap` is true (`onGap` is called): read the current state from the
  API again, then carry on. `bridge.events.poll({ since })` is the same replay as one JSON answer.
- Reading collections needs a `read` key; changing them needs the `paper` scope.
- There is no Parquet or DataFrame in Node: `candles.records()`, `candles.toCsv()` and plain arrays. Python has both.

## Browser apps

A page served from another origin (for example a Vite dev server on `http://localhost:5173`) must be listed in
`cors.allowedOrigins`. Never put an admin or live key in browser code.

<!-- docs/guides/collections.md -->

# Collections: lists of instruments and option universes

A **collection** is a named, tagged list of instruments. Make it once; downloads, recordings, spreadsheets and the Python
library can then say `collection: "nifty-weekly"` instead of pasting the same symbols again.

There are two kinds:

| Kind | What it holds | When the symbols are fixed |
|---|---|---|
| `static` | A list of symbols you chose, such as `NSE:RELIANCE`, `NSE:INFY` | Always |
| `option-universe` | A rule: "NIFTY, the current weekly expiry, 10 strikes each side of the at-the-money strike, calls and puts" | Never. It is worked out **each time it is used**, so the expiry rolls on and the at-the-money strike moves with the price |

Collections live in `collections.json` in your data folder (written safely: a temporary file, then a rename). They are part
of `mc-bridge backup`. Nothing in them is secret.

**Watchlists.** This version of the Bridge never had a watchlist store or watchlist routes (a `watchlists` section in the
config is refused as removed), so there is nothing to migrate. The Watchlist sheet in the Excel workbook is a list that lives in
the sheet. To use a collection in a sheet, see [In Excel and Google Sheets](#in-excel-and-google-sheets).

## Five minutes

```sh
# a key that may write (the paper scope; a read key can only read and resolve)
mc-bridge keys create --label collections --scope paper

export MCB_API_KEY=mcb_...
mc-bridge collections create banks --symbols NSE:HDFCBANK,NSE:ICICIBANK,NSE:SBIN --tags cash,banks
mc-bridge collections universe nifty-weekly --underlying NIFTY --expiries current-weekly --strikes atm:10 --tags options
mc-bridge collections resolve nifty-weekly        # the 43 symbols it means right now, and why
mc-bridge collections estimate nifty-weekly --interval 5m --days 30
```

The same through the API:

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/collections \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCB_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"nifty-weekly","tags":["options"],"kind":"option-universe",
       "universe":{"underlying":"NIFTY","expiries":"current-weekly","strikes":{"around":"atm","count":10},"sides":["CE","PE"],"includeUnderlying":true}}'

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCB_API_KEY" http://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/collections/nifty-weekly/resolve
```

## The option universe

```json
{
  "name": "nifty-weekly",
  "kind": "option-universe",
  "universe": {
    "underlying": "NIFTY",
    "expiries": "current-weekly",
    "strikes": { "around": "atm", "count": 10 },
    "sides": ["CE", "PE"],
    "includeUnderlying": true,
    "includeFuture": false
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `underlying` | An index or stock name without an exchange: `NIFTY`, `BANKNIFTY`, `SENSEX`, `RELIANCE` |
| `expiries` | `current-weekly`, `next-weekly`, `current-monthly`, `all-weekly`, or a list of dates such as `["2026-11-24","2026-12-01"]` |
| `strikes` | `{ "around": "atm", "count": 10 }`: that many **listed** strikes each side of the strike nearest the price. Or `{ "from": 24000, "to": 26000 }`: every listed strike between two prices (needs no price at all) |
| `sides` | `["CE","PE"]` (default), or just one |
| `includeUnderlying` | Add the index or stock itself (`NSE:NIFTY`). Default true |
| `includeFuture` | Add the future that expires in the month of each chosen expiry. Default false |

### How the expiry is chosen

The Bridge does not compute expiry dates. It reads the dates the exchange has **listed** (the instrument list) and chooses
among them, so a holiday shift is already in the date. The calendar is used only to explain what it sees.

| Rule | Means |
|---|---|
| `current-weekly` | The nearest listed expiry that has not closed. An expiry stops counting at 15:30 IST on its own day, so after the close the rule has already moved to the next one |
| `next-weekly` | The one after it |
| `current-monthly` | The nearest expiry that is the last of its calendar month |
| `all-weekly` | The nearest expiry and the weekly ones after it (about a week apart), at most `library.maxWeeklyExpiries` (5) |
| a list of dates | Exactly those. A date that is not listed, or has passed, is skipped with a warning that names the dates listed near it. If none is left, the answer is an error |

Weekly or monthly: an expiry is monthly when it is the last listed expiry of its month; the others are weekly. A stock, or an
index that has dropped its weeklies, has monthly expiries only. Asking such an underlying for `current-weekly` is an **error that says
so**; it never quietly uses a monthly date.

**Holiday shifts.** If the usual expiry day (say a Tuesday) is an exchange holiday, the exchange lists the day before. The
answer marks that expiry `shifted: true` with the reason (`2026-11-17 is a holiday`), and adds a warning. The listed date is used.

### How the strikes and the at-the-money strike are chosen

- The strikes are the ones the instrument list has for that underlying and expiry. `count` counts **listed** strikes, so a
  far strike listed at a wider step is still one strike, and the Bridge never invents a contract that does not exist.
- The at-the-money (ATM) strike is the listed strike nearest the price (the lower one on an exact tie). This is the rounding to
  the strike step: NIFTY lists every 50 points (25 026 gives 25 050), BANKNIFTY every 100 (52 340 gives 52 300), and a stock has
  its own step, usually 10 or 20 for a share near 1 400 (1 412 gives 1 420). The step of each expiry is in the answer (`step`).
- If no listed strikes are known at all (the instrument list has no options for it), an **index** gets a generated grid on
  its usual step (`library.strikeSteps`), the answer says `strikeSource: "grid"` and warns that some may not exist. A **stock** is never
  guessed: it is an error that tells you to refresh the list or set the step yourself.

### How honest it is about the price

An ATM needs the underlying's price. Every answer says where it came from in `atmSource`:

| `atmSource` | Meaning | When it is allowed |
|---|---|---|
| `not-needed` | The universe has explicit strikes (`from`, `to`) or is a static list | Always |
| `live` | A realtime price, not stale, market open | Always |
| `last-close` | Realtime class, but the market is closed or in pre-open, so the price is the last close and the ATM is yesterday's | Always, with a warning. A caller that needs a live ATM passes `requireLive` and gets an error instead |
| `supplied` | You passed `spot=<price>`: the ATM is worked out from it | Always, with a warning |
| `stale` | The Bridge itself marks the price stale (the feed fell behind) | Only with `allowStale=true`; otherwise an error (503) |
| `delayed`, `eod` | The price comes from a delayed or end-of-day source | Only with `allowStale=true`; otherwise an error (422). Such a price is never used for an ATM unless you say so |

With `allowStale` the answer is labelled and carries a plain warning. The dashboard's preview and the size estimate use it;
a download or a recording must not, so they call resolve at the moment they run, without it. Setting `library.allowStaleAtm`
to true makes labelled stale prices the default for callers that do not say (a spreadsheet request always says no).

## Using a collection

**Downloads and recordings** accept `collection: "<name>"` instead of `symbols`. They call `resolve` when the job runs, not
when it is made, so a nightly download of "NIFTY weekly, ATM +/- 10" means that night's expiry and that night's ATM.

**Size before you start**: `GET /v1/collections/{name}/estimate?intervals=5m,1d&days=30` gives rows, bytes (as CSV, about 70
a row) and broker calls (one per history chunk per symbol per interval: 60 days intraday, 2000 daily). It is an estimate: a
contract listed last week has less than 30 days, and a broker may keep less intraday history than you ask for.

**Usage**: `GET /v1/collections/{name}/usage` lists the downloads, recordings, auto-record rules and datasets that use the
collection. A kind marked `not-available` is kept by a part of the Bridge that is off, so it is not counted. Deleting a
collection that something **active** uses is refused (409) unless you add `force=true`.

### In Excel and Google Sheets

`/xl/quotes` takes `collection=` in place of `symbols=`:

```
http://127.0.0.1:4300/xl/quotes?collection=banks&fields=ltp,chg,pct&key=<your read-only key>
```

One request, one row per symbol, in the collection's order, with the usual freshness columns. An option universe is worked
out at the time of the request. For a sheet the price behind the ATM must be live, or the last close with the market shut; a
stale, delayed or end-of-day price answers a one-row table with the reason (the sheet shows it instead of old numbers). The
response headers `X-Collection-Resolved-At`, `X-Collection-Atm-Source`, `X-Collection-Rule` and `X-Collection-Warnings` say when and
how. A sheet request takes at most `integrations.xl.maxSymbols` symbols (100 by default): a universe that is bigger is
refused with the numbers. In Power Query or `IMPORTDATA` just use this address; in the workbook, replace the request's
`symbols=` part by `collection=<name>`.

### Tags

Tags are lower-case words (`weekly`, `nifty-options`; letters, digits and `_ . : -`, up to 32 characters, 20 per item). Filter
with `GET /v1/collections?tag=weekly,nifty` (a collection must have **every** tag). The datasets and downloaded files of the
downloads module use the same helper, so `GET /v1/datasets?tag=nifty` means the same thing.

## All the operations

| What | Request | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| List (filter by tag, kind, text) | `GET /v1/collections?tag=&kind=&q=` | read |
| One, with its symbols or universe | `GET /v1/collections/{name}` | read |
| Resolve now | `GET /v1/collections/{name}/resolve?allowStale=&requireLive=&spot=&priority=` | read |
| Size estimate | `GET /v1/collections/{name}/estimate?intervals=&days=` | read |
| Usage | `GET /v1/collections/{name}/usage` | read |
| Export (CSV or JSON) | `GET /v1/collections/{name}/export?format=csv\|json&resolved=` | read |
| Create | `POST /v1/collections` | paper |
| Change, tag, or **rename** | `PATCH /v1/collections/{name}` with any of `name`, `description`, `tags`, `symbols`, `universe` | paper |
| Copy | `POST /v1/collections/{name}/duplicate` with an optional `{ "name": "..." }` | paper |
| Import (CSV or JSON) | `POST /v1/collections/import` | paper |
| Delete | `DELETE /v1/collections/{name}?force=` | paper |

`{name}` may also be the collection's id (`col_...`). An **id never changes**. A **rename** keeps the id, and the old name keeps
finding the collection (the answer says `viaOldName`, with a warning), so a rule written with the old name does not break
the next morning. A new collection may take over an old name. Writing needs the `paper` scope: a read key reads and resolves only, and an
`admin`-only key cannot write either (the scope list is in [safety.md](safety.md)).

**Export and import.** JSON is the definition (a universe stays a universe) and imports back. CSV is the symbols, with the
columns `symbol,exchange,kind,underlying,expiry,strike,right`; for an option universe it is the symbols as they resolve now
(`X-Resolved-At`). To import a CSV, send it as `text/plain` with `?name=` (or as JSON `{ "format": "csv", "csv": "...",
"name": "..." }`); the symbols are in a column called `symbol`, or in the first column when there is no header. A spreadsheet's
leading apostrophe is removed. Everything is checked first: one bad line imports nothing, and the error names the line;
`skipInvalid=true` imports the rest. An existing name answers 409 unless `replace=true`.

```sh
mc-bridge collections export banks --format csv --out banks.csv     # never overwrites a file
mc-bridge collections import my-list.csv --tags imported
```

## For other parts of the Bridge

Downloads, the recorder and the rest read collections through `deps.library` (a contract service, `core/contracts.mjs`):

```js
const r = await deps.library.resolve("nifty-weekly", { requireLive: true, priority: "background", signal });
// r.symbols, r.resolvedAt, r.rule, r.atmSource, r.expiries, r.warnings
const e = await deps.library.estimate("nifty-weekly", ["5m"], 30);
deps.library.list({ tag: "options" });     // summaries
deps.library.get("nifty-weekly");           // the whole collection; throws NOT_FOUND
```

- Call `resolve` **when the job runs** (and again when it rolls over), with `priority: "background"` for bulk work and
  `requireLive: true` when a non-live ATM is not acceptable. Store the `resolvedAt` and the `rule` in the job's manifest.
- To appear in the usage view and to protect a collection from deletion, register a provider:
  `deps.library.registerUsageProvider("downloads", ({ id, name, names }) => [{ id, label, status, active }])`. `names` holds
  the name and its earlier names. Kinds: `downloads`, `recordings`, `rules`, `datasets`.
- Tags and names: `server/bridge/library/tags.mjs` has `normaliseTags`, `parseTagFilter`, `matchesTags`, `filterByTags` and
  `validateName`. A dataset keeps `tags: string[]` and a changeable name next to its fixed id, calls `normaliseTags` on write, and
  serves `?tag=` with `filterByTags`.
- Every write emits the bus topic `collection.changed` with `{ action: "created"|"updated"|"renamed"|"deleted", id, name, kind, tags, from? }`
  (never the symbol list).

## Settings

```json
"library": { "enabled": true, "maxCollections": 200, "maxSymbols": 5000, "maxWeeklyExpiries": 5, "allowStaleAtm": false,
             "strikeSteps": { "NIFTY": 50 } }
```

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | true | false switches the library off: every use answers a plain error |
| `maxCollections` | 200 | How many collections the store holds |
| `maxSymbols` | 5000 | Most symbols a collection may hold or resolve to |
| `maxWeeklyExpiries` | 5 | What `all-weekly` stops at |
| `allowStaleAtm` | false | Let a labelled stale, delayed or end-of-day price be the default for callers that do not say |
| `strikeSteps` | usual index steps | The step of a generated grid, used only when no listed strikes are known. Built in: NIFTY 50, BANKNIFTY 100, FINNIFTY 50, MIDCPNIFTY 25, SENSEX 100, BANKEX 100. A stock's step is never guessed |

## Limits, and what is not done

- A symbol is checked for **form** when it is saved (`NSE:RELIANCE`, `NFO:NIFTY-2026-11-24-25000-CE`), not against the broker's
  list: those lists change every day. A contract that has expired is kept and flagged with a warning when the collection is resolved.
- Expiry dates, strikes and lot sizes come from the instrument list your connected brokers give the Bridge. When it has not been
  loaded (no broker connected), a universe cannot be resolved and says so.
- The size estimate counts calendar days with the Bridge's holiday list (see `GET /v1/calendar/holidays`); it is not a promise of how
  much history a broker keeps.

---

<!-- docs/guides/excel-sheets.md -->

# Excel and Google Sheets

Prices and your own book in a spreadsheet, with **one request per refresh** instead of one per cell. Nothing a
spreadsheet can call is able to place, change or cancel an order: every `/xl` route is a read-only GET.

Fastest way: open the dashboard, **API > Integrations > Excel and Sheets**. Choose what to show, make a read-only key,
download the workbook (or copy the Apps Script), and press **Test it** to see the same single request a sheet makes,
with each price's freshness label.

| You use | What to use | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Excel for Windows | The workbook from the dashboard (or `node integrations/excel/make-template.mjs`) | Nothing else. `WEBSERVICE` exists only on Windows |
| Excel for Mac, Excel for the web | Power Query: [`quotes.pq`](../../integrations/excel/quotes.pq) | A refresh timer in Query Properties |
| Google Sheets | The Apps Script: [`bridge.gs`](../../integrations/google-sheets/bridge.gs) | A public address for the Bridge (see below) |

Microsoft's own page says `WEBSERVICE` is not available on Mac and does not list it for the web.

## The Excel workbook

Sheets: **Setup**, **Watchlist** (prices), **Positions**, **Holdings**, **Funds**, **Orders** and **Feed** (helper: each
request's address and answer). Choose the ones you want in the dashboard.

1. Make a key in the dashboard (read-only, expires) and paste it into the yellow cell on **Setup**, cell B6. Check the
   Bridge address in B5 (`http://127.0.0.1:4300` when Excel and the Bridge are on the same computer).
2. Open **Watchlist**. It already has ten symbols; type your own in column A (up to 50).
3. Press **F9**. The Status line on top says what happened, for example
   `OK. 10 prices, newest 2026-11-09 11:00:27 IST, oldest 0 s old.`

How it works: each sheet makes one request (`/xl/quotes`, `/xl/positions` and so on, as tab-separated text) into one
cell on **Feed**, cuts it into lines and fields with ordinary functions, and looks each row up by symbol. It works in
Excel 2013 and later on Windows. Functions newer than Excel 2007 (`WEBSERVICE`, `ENCODEURL`, `NUMBERVALUE`) are stored
with the `_xlfn.` prefix, which is what stops `#NAME?`. If you add your own formulas with these functions by typing
them in Excel, no prefix is needed; the prefix only matters inside the file.

Every price row says how current it is: **As of** (IST), **Age (s)**, **Class** (`realtime`, `delayed`, `eod`),
**Source** (`stream`, `cache`, `broker`) and **Stale**. In demo mode the Status line starts with `DEMO DATA`.

### A collection instead of typed symbols

`/xl/quotes` also takes `collection=<name>` in place of `symbols=`: a list you keep once in the Bridge (a fixed list, or an
option universe such as "NIFTY current weekly, ATM +/- 10", worked out at the time of the request). In Power Query or
`IMPORTDATA` use `/xl/quotes?collection=banks&fields=ltp,chg,pct`; in the workbook replace the `symbols=` part of the request.
A price that is not live is refused with the reason in a one-row table. See [collections.md](collections.md).

### The key

The workbook holds **no key** unless you tick "Put this key inside the workbook" when you download it; then the key is
stored as a workbook name (Formulas > Name Manager), not in a cell. Otherwise it lives in the yellow cell, and Setup
tells you whether a key is there. The key travels in the web address of each request, so it can appear in logs on the
way (this computer's own logs do not record it). Use a read-only key with an expiry, and **clear the cell before you
share or email the file**.

### Refreshing, and how often

| What | Recommended | How |
|---|---|---|
| Prices | Not more often than every 5 seconds | Press F9 (Setup switch "Refresh on every recalculation" = Yes), or Ctrl+Alt+F9 |
| Positions, Holdings, Funds, Orders | About once a minute | Same |
| Timer | Not built in: Excel has no timer without a macro | A macro below, or Power Query with *Refresh every N minutes* |

Each refresh is one request per sheet that is in the workbook. The Bridge allows each key about 50 requests a second
and your broker has its own limits, so a handful of requests every few seconds is nothing, while a macro that
recalculates in a loop is not. A macro for a 10-second timer (save the workbook as `.xlsm`; macros are yours to add,
the Bridge never ships one):

```vba
Sub Tick()
    Application.CalculateFull
    Application.OnTime Now + TimeSerial(0, 0, 10), "Tick"
End Sub
```

Run `Tick` once to start it. `Application.OnTime Now + TimeSerial(0,0,10), "Tick", , False` stops it.

### What a sheet costs, measured

On the demo Bridge, 42 symbols read one cell at a time (`/xl/ltp`, what the old workbook did) took 4.5 seconds cold
and about 1 broker call per symbol per recalculation; 120 cells recalculated in parallel got 66 answers `429`. The
same 42 symbols through `/xl/quotes` are one request, about 60 milliseconds, one batched read; 120 sheets in parallel
would still hit the per-key limit, and then the answer says how long to wait.

## Google Sheets

Google runs formulas and Apps Script on its own servers, which cannot reach `127.0.0.1`. The Bridge has to be
reachable from the internet through a tunnel you set up yourself: see [Exposing the Bridge](expose-alerts.md). Read
the risks there first: your data then passes through the tunnel provider and Google, your broker's terms may not allow
it ([compliance](compliance.md#tunnels-and-public-endpoints)), and requests that arrive through a tunnel are never
treated as coming from this computer, so the dashboard and every admin route refuse them.

Sheets formulas and Apps Script run on Google's servers and cannot reach `127.0.0.1`. Run `mc-bridge expose sheets`: it
turns on a separate **Sheets listener** (`server.sheetsIngress`, port 4302) that serves only `GET /xl/*`, only for
read-only keys, with its own host list and a request cap. Point your tunnel at that port and at nothing else (never at
4300); the dashboard, `/v1` and every admin route do not exist on it. Make a read-only key with an expiry, limited to the
accounts the sheet needs. Anyone with the address and the key can read your data, so do not share the sheet. The steps,
the safe layout and the check are in [expose-alerts.md](expose-alerts.md#6-google-sheets). If you tunnel to the main port
anyway, requests that arrive through a tunnel (a host from `server.allowedHosts`, or any `X-Forwarded-For` / `Forwarded` /
`CF-Connecting-IP` header) are never treated as coming from this computer, but a read key then reaches far more than a
sheet needs; `mc-bridge doctor` warns about it.

1. Make a key **for Google Sheets** in the dashboard (read-only, expires). It is sent in a request header, never in the
   address, so it stays out of tunnel and Google address logs. Do **not** use `IMPORTDATA(...&key=...)`: the key then sits
   in a web address everyone who can see the sheet can read.
2. *Extensions > Apps Script*, paste the script (button in the dashboard), save.
3. *Project Settings > Script properties*: `BRIDGE_URL` (your tunnel address, no trailing slash) and `BRIDGE_KEY`.
   Anyone who can edit the script can read these: do not share the sheet.
4. Reload the sheet. **Bridge > Set up sheets** makes Watchlist, Positions, Holdings, Funds and Orders;
   **Bridge > Refresh now** fills them (one request per sheet); **Bridge > Start timed refresh** runs it every 5 minutes
   (1, 5, 10, 15 and 30 are the intervals Google allows).
5. Or use `=BRIDGE_QUOTES(A5:A30)` in any cell: the whole range in one request, with the freshness columns.

Google's own limits (Apps Script quotas page): 20,000 URL Fetch calls a day for a consumer account (100,000 for
Workspace), 90 minutes a day of trigger run time on a consumer account, 30 seconds for a custom function. One refresh
is at most five requests, so every minute is about 7,200 a day. Every 5 minutes is plenty for a book, and gentler on
your broker.

## The routes (for Power Query, curl, your own script)

All are `GET`, all take `?format=csv|tsv|json` (CSV is the default; CRLF for CSV, LF for TSV; numbers with a `.`
decimal point and no thousands separator; times in IST as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`) and the optional `?cache=1`.

| Route | What |
|---|---|
| `/xl/quotes?symbols=A,B,C&fields=ltp,chg,pct,volume` | One row per symbol, in the order asked, duplicates kept. At most 100 symbols (`integrations.xl.maxSymbols`, up to 200). `fields` chooses value columns from `ltp open high low close chg pct volume oi bid ask`; `as_of age_s class source stale error` always follow. A bad symbol gives blank values and a text in `error`: it never fails the table |
| `/xl/positions`, `/xl/holdings`, `/xl/funds`, `/xl/orders` | Your book, fixed columns. Every account the key may use that can answer, or `?account=`. An account that cannot answer (not logged in) gives one row with its name and an `error` |
| `/xl/instrument?symbol=NSE:RELIANCE&field=lot` | One symbol and one field: a bare number. Several symbols or fields: a table of `lot tick freeze name kind` |
| `/xl/ltp`, `/xl/quote`, `/xl/chain`, `/xl/history` | Unchanged: one value (`#N/A` on error), the option chain, candles |

Rules these routes keep:

- **Never a backup price.** A Yahoo-style or other backup source is never used (`?backup=true` is refused), and the
  single-value routes also refuse a price whose class is not `realtime`, because a bare number cannot carry the label.
  `/xl/quotes` shows such a value with its `class` and `stale` columns instead.
- **Read-only.** A `?key=` in the address works only on `/xl`, and only for keys that can do nothing but read. Keys are
  never logged.
- **Caching is off by default** (`Cache-Control: no-store`). With `?cache=1` a table is sent with
  `Cache-Control: private, max-age=5` (`integrations.xl.cacheSeconds`) and an `ETag`; `If-None-Match` gets `304`.
  Errors are never cached.
- **Errors you can read in a cell.** A refused table request answers a one-row table
  `status,code,message,retry_after_s`, for example `429,RATE_LIMITED,Too many refreshes: wait 3 seconds and try again.,3`,
  with the real status and a `Retry-After` header.

## When something is wrong

| You see | Why | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `#NAME?` in a cell | A workbook made before this version, or a formula typed from an old example, stored without the `_xlfn.` prefix | Download the workbook again. In your own formulas, type them in Excel (it adds the prefix itself) |
| Status `NO ANSWER` | The request failed: the Bridge is not running, the address or key is wrong or expired, the symbol list made the address longer than 2,048 characters, or the Bridge answered 429 | Check Setup (address, key check line), open the address in a browser or press **Test it** in the dashboard, wait 10 seconds and press F9. `WEBSERVICE` cannot show the reason; the dashboard test and Power Query can |
| Prices blank in the morning | Your broker session expired overnight, so the Bridge has nothing to read. The table says `SESSION_EXPIRED` in the Error column | Log in on the Accounts page; press F9 |
| `429` / "Too many refreshes: wait N seconds" | Too many requests from one key (about 50 a second), or your broker's limit | Refresh less often; one sheet is one request, so look for a macro or a loop |
| `Stale` = true, or `Class` = `delayed` | The value is older than the Bridge's target, or comes from a delayed feed | Do not trade on it; the `As of` time says how old. Press F9 once the market feed is back |
| `DEMO DATA` | The Bridge is in demo mode: sample prices | Expected until a real broker is connected |
| `symbol could not be priced` | A typo, an expired contract or a symbol your broker does not carry | Bridge symbols: `NSE:RELIANCE`, `NSE:M&M`, `NFO:NIFTY-2026-11-24-FUT`. Search with `GET /v1/instruments/search` |
| `401` on a table, key was working | The key expired or was revoked | Make a new one; the dashboard shows expiries under API > Keys |
| Excel for Mac or the web shows nothing | No `WEBSERVICE` there | Use `quotes.pq` (Power Query) or Google Sheets |

## Power Query (Windows and Mac)

Power Query sends the key in an `Authorization` header, so a plain read key is enough and it never appears in an
address. [`quotes.pq`](../../integrations/excel/quotes.pq) reads the ranges `BridgeURL`, `BridgeKeyCell` and
`WatchlistSymbols` that the workbook defines; [`history.pq`](../../integrations/excel/history.pq) and
[`chain.pq`](../../integrations/excel/chain.pq) read candles and the option chain. Paste one into *Data > Get Data >
Blank Query > Advanced Editor*, choose **Anonymous** when asked how to connect, and set *Refresh every N minutes* in
Query Properties.

## Sharing a template

`node integrations/excel/make-template.mjs my-template.xlsx` writes the same workbook with a sample watchlist and no
key. Send it to a friend; they paste their own key. For Sheets, the script's *Bridge > Set up sheets* builds the same
layout in any blank sheet.

## Formula safety

Text that begins with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return is prefixed with `'` in CSV, TSV and JSON, so
Excel never evaluates text that came from a broker or an instrument master.
